# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

## claude-artifacts
Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. Call guide before the first publish of a session: it holds the rules a page must meet. This server cannot change who can see an artifact (sharing, publishing to the web, unsharing), delete an artifact or read view counts; say so instead of calling a tool. # Second delegated rulings — 2026-10-28 (the user: "use your own best judgement, fix the remaining issues, name whatever you need yourself")

Marker for every edit: *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling Rn)* or *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
In-text record: "Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling Rn (user delegated all remaining calls, including naming the reference machine): ...".
G1-G5 and R1-R10 of rr-rulings.md stay binding except where amended below. R11 (X14 stays open) is SUPERSEDED by R12.

## G6 Cross-GDD edits are now allowed
A blocker that needs a sibling GDD to change is fixed IN the sibling. Owner wins (G1): the registry `source:` GDD, else the publisher of the field/signal, keeps its value; the other conforms. Each file has exactly one writer per pass; requests to another file go to that file's writer.
Classify every blocker first: **CONFLICT** (the same thing has two values/contracts in two GDDs) -> the owner's value stands and the other GDD conforms; **GAP** (the owner lacks a surface, exemption, field or signal that a consumer's user-ruled or delegated-ruled behaviour requires, e.g. Interaction's act_gate exempt list lacking self-patch, HUD lacking a give_up surface) -> the OWNER ADDS it, and the consumer's requirement is the spec. Never "fix" a gap by removing the consumer's ruled behaviour.
Precedence: where R1 text conflicts with R13/R14, R13/R14 win; re-mark such text "delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14".

## R12 Reference machines and build (closes X14; supersedes R11)
- **RM-DESKTOP (minimum-spec desktop):** Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class (Vulkan 1.2+); SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms.
- **RM-DECK (handheld):** Steam Deck LCD (2022), SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 33.3 ms.
- **Build type for every wall-clock figure:** a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus` (project.godot), vsync on, the pipeline's warm-up of 120 frames, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result.
- **P99 headroom:** pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (headroom >= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck).
- The developer's machine is not a reference machine; figures from it are indicative only.
- Recorded in `project.yaml` as `qa.min_spec` (done by the orchestrator). In GDDs: replace "X14 open / not named / [blocked: reference hardware]" with the named machines; performance ACs become gated on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK at the spike (still measured at the spike, so a value not yet measured is "pending spike", not "blocked").

## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

## R15 OQ-52: confirmed option (a)
A `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt from the fairness step-back. Confirmed; drop "USER DECISION".

## R16 OQ-DO-30: option (A)
The playtest preset registers only `debug_overlay_mark`; `debug_overlay_reveal` is dev-only. A tester session can never leave `HIDDEN`. Update DO-2/6/8, AC-DO-170, AC-DO-185.

## R17 Interaction OQ 48: confirmed
A wounded victim is not guaranteed an escape (Pillar 3, honest horror). Confirmed; no cooldown or damage floor.

## R18 Player Controller OQ 29(ii): pre-ruled conditional
If the target-acquisition spike fails and the lighter fallbacks do not close the gap, `aim_indicator` defaults ON for mouse players (still player-toggleable). Until then D9 (off by default) stands.

## R19 Boarding OQ-BS-34 fallback: pre-ruled conditional
If the boarding spike finds no K3 pass line inside 21-28 tiles with Attention's levers, the X3 route band's upper end widens to 31 tiles for the reference sortie (lower end stays 21). Not applied now; the spike decides.

## R20 Every "default applied, pending user confirmation" is confirmed
Every item marked "Default applied ... pending user confirmation" or "(confirm)" in any GDD is confirmed as of 2026-10-28 by delegation. Re-mark it "confirmed 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R20" and remove it from open user-decision lists. Do not change the value.

## R21 Remaining "USER DECISION" items
Any other "USER DECISION" left in a GDD is decided by its creative-director lean (G2) or, absent one, by the option that preserves prior user rulings and needs the least new content; record it as delegated ruling R21 with one sentence of reason. Never leave a "USER DECISION" open.

# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.
- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.
- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.
- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.
- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.
- R9 Undesigned dependencies (VS/Alpha systems with no GDD): not a blocker; keep them listed as "undesigned — provisional contract" with the interface this GDD assumes.
- R10 Pending-confirmation defaults and PLACEHOLDER values are not changed by these rulings unless a blocker shows them internally inconsistent.
- R11 X14 (reference machine) stays OPEN: never name or invent a reference machine, build type or spec anywhere.

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria

Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.

- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

133:**LS-10 — Failure lifecycle: six states, five severities.** States: `0 OK` (`hp ≥ HP_OK`, no forced mode), `1 DEGRADED` (`HP_FAIL < hp < HP_OK`; `eff` from D.4; hazard modes may be active; with none active the subject carries mode WORN, LS-11 — the module-body trace *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*), `2 FAILED` (`hp ≤ HP_FAIL` or `forced_mode ≠ 0`; no function; leaks continue; repairable), `3 DESTROYED` (`hp` = 0; permanent scrap; repair rejected `NOT_REPAIRABLE`; salvage then replace), `4 SALVAGED` (removed by `salvage_node`; tombstone slot; fluid ports `open_end`), `5 ABSENT` (never populated; inert; no ports connected; no descriptors). Severity `sev` 0..4 from D.4 (0 none; 1 trace — the weep, the flicker, the frost on the lagging; 2 minor; 3 major — hazard to nearby play, first `alarm_eligible` level; 4 critical — arcing, jetting, runaway), raised by hazard rules (breach `A_hole` ≥ 32 → 4; OVERLOAD `ρ` > 1000 → ≥ 1 from the first step over (LS-11) and `ρ` ≥ 1500 → 3; any forced mode → ≥ 3). Damage is monotonic per cause; repair raises `hp` only through `repair_step` up to `hp_cap`. The complete transition table is in *States and Transitions*.

212:*Rule (phase 9, per NODE, EDGE and SEAM).* The subject's **dominant descriptor** is its live descriptor of highest `sev` (ties to the lowest `mode` id); `mode_key` = `(mode << 3) | sev` of that descriptor, 0 when none has `sev ≥ 1` (a u8, since `mode` ≤ 27 and `sev` ≤ 4; the boot assertion `GRAPH_BOOT_MODE_ID` refuses a build whose largest mode id exceeds 31, because `(mode << 3) | sev` would otherwise truncate silently — widening is a schema bump) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. On each run phase 9 computes the key from the run's state and compares it with the persisted `mode_key`. If they differ, then `mode_since_step` = `step_no` (0 when the new key is 0), `mode_key` = the new key, and, when `isolated_at_step` > 0, `isolated_at_step` = `step_no` too (so `grow_steps` is 0 and never negative). The key does **not** change when a closed valve drops `intensity_pm` to 0 (isolation changes the flow, not the mode or `sev`), so isolation only stamps `isolated_at_step` (LS-11). A SEAM's `mode_since_step` starts at its `built_step`. A cascade-forced mode (`forced_mode_next` applied in phase 0) changes the key at the next phase 9 like any other change. Because `mode_key` is persisted, a snapshot taken on any tick restores to the same key and no restamp occurs on load.
214:*Worked example (default tuning).* A coolant PIPE wears: `hp` falls below `HP_OK`, WORN sev 1 from step 1,000 (`warn_since_step` 1,000, key (10 << 3) | 1 = 81, `mode_since_step` 1,000). At step 1,500 `hp` falls below `LEAK_HP`: LEAK, say sev 2, key (1 << 3) | 2 = 10, `mode_since_step` 1,500, so `mode_steps` is 0 on the first LEAK run while `since_steps` is already 500. At step 1,620 the leak reaches sev 3 (key 11): `mode_since_step` 1,620, `mode_steps` 0. At step 1,700 the player closes the upstream valve: `intensity_pm` falls to 0, `isolated_at_step` 1,700, `grow_steps` = 1,700 − 1,620 = 80 and stays 80 at step 1,900 while `mode_steps` reads 280 (dullness keeps ageing, extent does not grow). The valve reopens at step 2,000: `isolated_at_step` 0, `grow_steps` = 2,000 − 1,620 = 380 — the one-time extent step bounded by the edge that Failure & Trail's FT-8 documents. A breach cascade restamps on its own sev rise, so the bent rib of Failure & Trail's ET-3 starts at its source with `grow_steps` 0.
256:**LS-21 — Serialization, hash, summary, interchange.** *Persisted (canonical):* `schema_version`, `next_node_id`, `next_edge_id`, `next_seam_id`, `next_section_id`, `last_step_no` and the per-hook cursors `last_step_power`, `last_step_atmo`, `last_step_failure` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the `def_table` CSR pair (`def_off`, `def_utf8`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; nodes and edges with every field of LS-3/LS-5 including tombstones; SeamRecords; sections with `dormant`, `dormant_since_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, `rate_pm`, `stress_pm`, `stress_until_step`, `vented_mgu`, `radiated_dj`, `spilled_cool_ml`, `produced_mgu`, `breathed_mgu`, `produced_dj`, `burned_uml`, `spilled_heat_mdj` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `discarded_*`, `withdrawn_*` (M16, per medium) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)*; compartments `layout_room_ref`, `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `T`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle_ml` and the hysteresis memory `band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t`, `p_prev` (the previous run's `P`), and the warn trackers `warn_since_o2`, `warn_since_p`, `warn_since_t` (i32 each) and `warn_bits` (u8) — canonical order after `p_prev` (+13 bytes per compartment, 65 for the MVP five) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; every stored OPENING's `strain_gas` and `strain_heat` live bits (SEAL_STRAIN hysteresis, D.14); **and the three input queues** — `pending_draw` (compartment, crew, mGU), `pending_load` (node, `req_w`) and `pending_trace` (kind, subject, magnitude), each in arrival order and bounded (draw ≤ `MAX_CREW` × compartments, load ≤ 64, trace ≤ `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`), plus the last applied `draw_grant` table. A snapshot can be taken on any tick, so a queue that held a breath, a trace or a load change between two hook ticks would otherwise be lost on restore and the restored run would diverge from the uninterrupted one *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Derived, never in a snapshot:* `V`, `exposed_tiles` (from Layout), components, trees, `path_cap`, degrees, id → slot maps, `served_pm`, descriptors, `P`/`p_o2`/`o2_pm`, last-emitted buckets, the cached hash. Rule: anything the next step depends on that is not re-derivable from persisted fields is persisted (`t_rem`, `tc_rem`, `fuel_rem`, `out_w`, `forced_mode_next`, `warn_since_step` with its `has_warn` bit, `thaw_until_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, the GA-T fields `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step`, `dormant_since_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, the three `pending_*` queues, the band and SEAL_STRAIN memory, the compartment warn trackers `warn_since_o2/p/t` and `warn_bits` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); `served_pm` is not, because phase 2 recomputes it before use. `canonical_bytes()` = the persisted fields in a fixed documented order, each as `[u32 tag][u32 length][field.to_byte_array()]`, raw slot arrays with tombstones — native memcpy, no interpreted loop. **`block_hash()`** is published: cached, recomputed only when the block was written since the last hash, H64 over `canonical_bytes()` (H64 = the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 that native `HashingContext` returns, read as a little-endian u64 — a truncated hash, never a hand-rolled 64-bit mix) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the kernel's `state_hash` is registered as `state_hash(scope, T) = H64( T || world_seed || concat over b in scope sorted by block_id of (len(block_id) || block_id || schema_version || len(canonical_bytes(b)) || block_hash(b)) )` with `block_hash(b) = H64(canonical_bytes(b))` cached per block and invalidated by the dirty bit, and the Graph's `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` feed it unchanged *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*. The one-level Merkle form (`state_hash` over per-block cached hashes, H64 via native `HashingContext` or S0-d's winner) is **kernel amendment K-1, routed to the kernel owner as an ADR candidate** and not a rule of this GDD (R5). **SHARED_SUMMARY** (VS-B): per compartment `T_dC` (int16, 0.1 °C), `P` (u16), `p_o2` (u16), three bands (3 bits each); per node/edge `state` (3 bits) + `sev` (3 bits) + `served_q` (0..15); per loop component `pool_q`; active descriptors compact `(id, mode, sev, alarm_eligible, intensity bucket = intensity_pm / 100, since_steps, mode_steps, grow_steps, each saturating at 2^24 − 1)` — 7 bytes for the first six fields plus 3 bytes for each of the two GA-T ages, 13 bytes each, from which a client derives `fail_since_step` and the trail's own age so two MIRROR crewmates see equal trail extent, dullness and density (CR-10, VS-B) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from failure-and-trail-system; GA-T fields added 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; seam list; about 0.4 KB at MVP, deltas ride the dirty keys; clients never receive `t_rem`, queues or RNG inputs — they receive truth, quantised. **Interchange (S-1, routed to Save/Load):** every Graph value stays below 2^53; the canonical form is packed int arrays; any JSON text form must carry the raw canonical bytes as base64 (`Marshalls.raw_to_base64`); `var_to_bytes` is not used — the `allow_objects` argument of the first draft is Godot 3-era and does not exist in 4.x, and Variant framing would put engine-version headers inside the hashed form *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; never a `Resource` for saves (R6; Godot JSON parses numbers as float — TD, sourced). Restore is two-phase (decode and validate into a scratch state, then swap); `restore(data, stored_version)` supports exactly version 1 in MVP, any other version is a reported failure, and every failure is a named `GRAPH_RESTORE_*` reason with the live state untouched (Section E). Type ids are append-only forever — the only forward-compatibility promise v1 makes.
279:**LS-25 — Endogenous rates: wear, compression, stress.** Everything that damages a subject without a player or a horror doing it is one of: overload (D.9) and the short burn of a FAILED cable in SHORT (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, wear on period steps (LEAK, OVERHEAT, fatigue, patch decay, and **duty** — `W_DUTY_BP_PER_100` on every running SCRUBBER, PUMP, REACTOR and HEATER, D.9, so that a fully repaired ship is quiet for a session but never permanently safe (P5): at 2 bp per period a healthy machine reaches `HP_OK` after 1500 periods = 4.2 h of continuous duty and carries WORN from then on *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*), thaw-burst (C5). All of it is multiplied by the section's `rate_pm` (HOME 1000; DERELICT `10^6 / DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION` = 2000, so a derelict fault's wear clock runs at half length; clocks set by a stock draining — a tank emptying, a pool venting — do not compress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* and by `stress_pm` (`BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` 2000 while the section is stressed by M17 STRESS, 1000 otherwise). The multipliers never touch gas exchange, heat conduction or supply: the breach rhythm makes the ship *fail* faster, not *leak* faster — the hole still sets the hiss. On a derelict, faults that are "dead" (dried trails) are authored as subjects at `hp` ≤ `HP_FAIL` with a `def_id` whose module is powered-off, so they emit descriptors with `intensity_pm` 0 and `since_steps` large (the dried trail) and only wake when power or coolant reaches them.

17	## Summary
18	
19	The Failure & Trail System is the pure-reader renderer that turns the Life-Support Graph's failure descriptors into physical marks on the ship (mist, frost fan, scorch, puddle, hairline -> crack -> bent rib), in three sizes, thickest at the source, with density from flow and length from age; it holds no state, registers no block, hook or command, writes only canvas, material and particle output, and is the truth channel that no hallucination may add to, alter or remove. Read this GDD if you design, art-direct or build anything that shows a fault, tells a player where a fault is, lights a fault, or sits beside the trails (Emitter State, Lighting, the Perception Filter, Horror Entities, In-World Instruments, Onboarding, Derelict Authoring): it fixes the descriptor-to-visual table of record for all eighteen descriptor ids (ids 1-10, 20-26 and 27 PATCH_WEEP; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review*), the growth, reach, dullness and budget formulas with their worked values, the tell-window and faster-than-walking invariants, and its acceptance criteria (AC-1 to AC-188, with lettered splits; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*). It does not simulate propagation or atmosphere, plays no sound, and has no UI of its own.
20	
21	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` (systems-index enumeration #9, Recommended Design Order 8; Category Gameplay) · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Life-Support Graph`, `Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera` (both designed); `Command & Simulation Layer` (designed, transitive); `Ship Section & Layout Data Model` (designed, hard: anchor geometry and room surfaces, LY-8 and LY-23). Depended on by: Onboarding (index, undesigned) and Emitter State (EM-17, soft, designed); neighbours that repeat this system's rows: Lighting, Perception Filter, Horror Entities, In-World Instruments, Adaptive Audio, Interaction, Derelict Authoring, Sanity, Boarding & Salvage, Modular Ship Assembly, Suit & HUD (all designed); still undesigned: Onboarding, Settings, Co-op. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: neighbour statuses refreshed.)*
22	
23	## Overview
24	
25	The Failure & Trail System turns the Life-Support Graph's failure descriptors into physical marks on the ship: it is the **skin that shows the bruise**. It is a pure reader and a pure renderer. Every frame it reads the Graph's true failure state (`failures()` descriptors, the compartment bands and true temperature, `fuel_puddle_ml`) through the one read channel `read_view`, and draws, for each descriptor that has a consequence-channel medium, a mark in that loop's own vocabulary at the fitting, seam, opening frame or rib where the failure sits: **mist drifts** where air escapes, a **static crystalline frost fan** where coolant weeps, a **sharp radial scorch** where power arcs or a machine overheats, a **glossy, flat, ember-edged puddle** where fuel drips, a **hairline that becomes a crack and then a bent rib** where the hull gives. Every mark is thickest at its source, in one of three sizes (48, 96 and 144 base px) chosen by severity, with density chosen by flow and length chosen by age. The system holds no state: it registers no block, no step hook and no command, owns no propagation and no atmosphere (both are Graph state), writes only `CanvasItem`, `Material` and particle properties, and every visual property of every mark is a pure function of the Graph's current values and the render clock. That statelessness is what makes it a **truth channel**: a trail is on the Graph's closed consequence-channel list, so the Perception Filter may neither remove, alter nor add one, and a hallucination that lies about a machine's sprite or gauge cannot lie about the floor beside it.
26	
27	The player never operates this system and never sees a menu for it. They meet it as the ship's handwriting. They wake in the cryo bay and their chest lamp catches a frost fan running from a lagged elbow toward the far wall; they follow it to its thickest point and find the fitting; they close the valve and watch the drip stop while the fan stays, still and dulling; they weld on a derelict section and watch mist spread along the seam bead; they hear a hiss behind a dark panel and walk to it because the mist will be there once the lamp arrives. Trails are the visible half of the Graph's two-channel warning: the fairness gate guarantees that a sev >= 1 descriptor exists for at least `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (10 s) before any endogenous loss, and this system is what makes that descriptor *seen* **where the descriptor is on the consequence channel** (the FREEZE, BREACH, OVERLOAD, OVERHEAT-shimmer and seam-weep pre-stages, and the PATCH_WEEP of a patched subject; a wearing LEAK's own pre-stage is still the WORN descriptor, which is module-body and drawn by the module presenter, not here: FT-7, FT-32) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, with a growth rate bounded so a far-elbow trail crosses a six-tile room (288 base px) inside the 10-30 s tell window, and so a sev-4 trail on a single edge is strictly faster than walking and no faster than running. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the growth promises are measured from the trail's own per-mode onset, the Graph's GA-T, which the Graph adopted in LS-14 (FT-8, FT-30).)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The same grammar, dulled and stilled, is the verdict of a dead derelict: a frost fan with no leak is coolant, a radial scorch at a junction box is power, an ember-edged stain is fuel, branching hairlines through ribs are the hull, and nothing at all where the air went.
28	
29	The index describes the system as a pure reader that maps "graph failure state and footprint sources" to trail visuals. This GDD reconciles the second half: the Graph persists no footprint record and emits no footprint-tagged descriptor (the M17 `deposit_trace` kinds surface only as ordinary hp, temperature and section-rate changes), so this system draws **Graph descriptors only**; a hidden entity's web-grammar marks (smear, branching rime, dust direction, filament twitch) belong to Horror Entities and share only the floor-marks draw band. Without this system the Graph is invisible: Pillar 1's design test ("a hidden stat vs a visibly leaking pipe -> the pipe") has no pipe to draw, the tell Pillar 2 promises is a number nobody sees, and Pillar 4's guarantee that "no lie is unfalsifiable" has no physical witness to check a false gauge against. The MVP hypothesis (`design/gdd/game-concept.md`, MVP item 2: "a visible O2 / heat / power graph with propagating, physically rendered failures") cannot be tested without it. It is a Feature-layer system (it holds a render of Core state, not state) with three designed hard dependencies, the Life-Support Graph, the Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera and the Ship Section & Layout Data Model (LY-8, LY-23), whose anchor geometry and room surfaces this system reads (Dependencies). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Layout is designed.)* The MVP slice (what ships first and what waits) is FT-38.
30	
31	*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (-> `/architecture-decision`): the split between the notification handler and the render callback (PR-8 rule 3); stepped sprite frames vs `GPUParticles2D` for moving media (spike-gated); the per-instance reveal-threshold and coverage-rank plumbing that keeps alpha binary; a pure `RefCounted` resolver `descriptor -> TrailSpec` so the decision logic is headless-testable; z-index numbering inside the floor-marks band; and the Perception Filter's truth-channel mask route (Filter-owned).*
32	
33	## Player Fantasy
34	
35	**Framing: direct, with a forensic depth and a witness guarantee.** The player knowingly reads failure as marks the ship leaves on itself and follows them to their source. *(creative-director consulted; Framing A "follow the mark to the wound" adopted, with B "the room remembers" as its depth in the past tense and C "the one thing you can still trust" as its guarantee. The Graph adopted the same layered shape; here the direct layer is the player's own act of reading.)*

36	
37	> The ship cannot speak, but it cannot lie. When a loop fails, the failure writes itself onto the hull in the loop's own hue: soft drifting mist where air escapes, a static crystalline frost fan where coolant weeps, a sharp radial scorch where power arcs, a glossy ember-edged puddle under a fuel flange, a hairline that becomes a crack and then a bent rib where the hull gives. Every mark is thickest at its source. The player's chest lamp finds it; their eye follows it; their hands end at the fitting that failed.
38	>
39	> Competence is reading. A veteran crew is not faster with a wrench; it sees the frost the moment the pipe lets go (the frost fan is the first thing the loop draws, and it can precede the wall gauge's reading), knows a scorch from a stain, and knows an old isolated leak (still, dulled, no drip) from a live one. On a dead derelict the same marks are a verdict: frost fan, coolant; radial scorch, power (conditional on the Graph emitting a dead electrical descriptor: ET-4, Open Questions); ember stain, fuel; branching hairlines, the hull; and nothing at all where the air went (the O2 verdict is carried by the ATMO band and the draught, not by a mark: default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), Open Questions 6b) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "sees the frost before the gauge drops" had no mechanism, because a wearing pipe carries only the WORN descriptor, which this system never draws and the Filter may corrupt; the claim is now "the moment the pipe lets go". Whether a consequence-channel sev-1 sweat companion exists for WORN is routed to the Graph owner.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: reading before failure is true only for some failures, and the fantasy now says which. **A floor pre-stage exists** (drawn here, consequence channel, readable before the loss) for: a freezing pipe (`4 FREEZE` sev 1), a hull plate or seam giving way (`5 BREACH` hairline, sev 1-2), a cable or box warming (`7 OVERLOAD`, sev 1-2), a machine heating (`3 OVERHEAT` shimmer, sev 2), a new weld (the seam weep), a strained hatch (`26`) and a **patched** pipe, duct or cable (`27 PATCH_WEEP`, the small weep that tells the patch is still only a patch). **No floor pre-stage exists** for the most common failure, a wearing pipe, duct or tank before it lets go (a `1 LEAK` that has not yet crossed `LEAK_HP`, or a `2 SHORT` not preceded by OVERLOAD): its only earlier tells are on the module-body channel (sprite wear, gauge), which the Filter may corrupt, so there the floor tells the truth only after the line has let go. Whether the Graph adds a consequence-channel sweat companion for WORN is the open Pillar 2 / Pillar 4 decision of Open Questions 45, owed to the Graph owner; until it is ruled the fantasy promises "reads the moment it lets go" for a wearing pipe and "reads before" only for the list above.)*
40	>
41	> And the floor never lies. When sanity slips, the gauge can read green, the scrubber can spin, the pipe's edge can bleed violet; the mist at its outlet does not change. No hallucination adds, alters or removes a mark. When the machine and the floor disagree, the floor wins.
42	
43	**Emotion.** *Dread-literacy.* The player is a tracker reading a wounded body. The power is not control and not speed; it is **certainty earned by looking**: the click of following a mark back to the fitting that made it. Under threat that certainty is the only one the crew has left. The Graph's fantasy is caretaking under threat (the circulation); this system's is the skin that shows the bruise. In the Pillar 1 voice: *"Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth."* and *"Physical consequences. A pipe may look fixed, but the room still gets cold, the air still thins, the pressure still drops."* (partial quotation by design: the concept's human-channel bullet for Pillar 1 pre-dates the chest-mounted lamp decision and is not quoted here). Design test from the concept: *a hidden stat vs a visibly leaking pipe -> the pipe*; and from the visual anchor: *a "COOLANT LOW" banner vs a frosted elbow with a drip -> the elbow.*
44	
45	**MDA and motivation.** Primary aesthetic: Challenge, delivered as competence by literacy (reading faster, not repairing faster). *(The concept ranks Discovery first and Challenge second at game level; this system ranks Challenge first locally because its job is the concept's Challenge row, a visible life-support graph that fails in traceable ways, while the verdict grammar, ET-4, delivers Discovery; this is not drift.)* Secondary: Discovery (the verdict grammar on derelicts: "what killed this ship?"). Tertiary: Fellowship (the floor is common ground two crewmates can both point at; **conditional on the VS-B MIRROR path**, which is not in the MVP: at MVP, single-player, Fellowship is a promise and not a delivered aesthetic *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*). Competence is served by legible cause, traceable origin and no hidden threshold; autonomy by a mark that tells the player what is *true* and never what to *do* (valve, patch, retreat or ignore stays theirs); relatedness by identical trails on every client, which lets crewmates verify each other (a VS-B property; see the Dependencies row for Co-op).
46	
47	**Anchor moment: the first mark (cryo bay, minute one).** You wake. Your chest lamp (beam origin = the per-facing `chest_point`, hands free) falls across the deck and catches a fan of Coolant Ice frost running from a lagged elbow to the far wall. Nothing in the room moves faster than the drip at its root. Your eye does the work before you do: the fan is thickest at the elbow, so you walk to it. You close the upstream valve: the drip stops, but the fan stays, **still, not gone** (the Graph's isolated-leak descriptor has `intensity_pm` 0 while its mode stays, `LSG:127`). The heater warms the bay (8 mC per Graph step, about 2.5 minutes to COMFORT, `LSG:839`) and the fan's reach pulls back toward a local stamp at the elbow, while the coolant wet run, which owes nothing to temperature, stays on the floor from the elbow to the far wall and keeps the way back to the wound *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The wall gauge finally agrees with the pipe. The tutorial is physical, and the fixture is authored so the leak's mode onset (`mode_since_step`, GA-T) is already at least 56 steps old when you arrive, so the frost already reaches the far wall at wake (the self-contained fixture `FX-CRYO` is owned by this GDD, FT-40; a flagged requirement on the Onboarding GDD, see Open Questions). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the fixture authors the mode onset, not `fail_since_step`, which belongs to FAILED nodes and is not what a LEAK counts from.)* Feel: quiet competence, "I read that."
48	
49	**Experience targets (retained-capture scenes; every number is a locked value or a flagged placeholder).**

On a single edge, walk and the front passes you; run and you keep ahead of it. **What moves, and what does not** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the l head (the bent rib) stays at the source, because the chain tapers (FT-6, D.1), so what travels along the edge is the narrowing tail of s-sized pieces, mostly a hairline; and the front is the **extent of the mark, which is its age, not a hazard boundary**: nothing becomes dangerous because the mark reached it (the hazard is the descriptor's own `sev` and flow, the Graph's). You can count the wounds the crew survived, as marks that are *true*, not as a score | Isolated leaks keep their mode with `intensity_pm` 0 (`LSG:127`); seam weeps persist until wear-in (`LSG:170`); FT-17. A patched pipe is **not** one of these: it carries the small PATCH_WEEP, see the anti-promises and FT-32 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
59	
60	*Session emotional arc carried by trails:* calm reading (ET-1) -> watchful tending (ET-2) -> forensic curiosity (ET-4) -> flight (ET-3) -> vertigo and grip (ET-5) -> ownership by history (ET-6). Flow entry is ET-1's single trail. The intentional flow breaks are the s -> m -> l jumps: a severity change is a discrete `F/` key event, so the jump is sudden by construction (FT-6).
61	
62	**Design test.** *When a choice makes a failure easier to notice from a marker vs easier to follow from the mark it leaves on the ship -> the mark. When a choice makes a trail more dramatic vs keeps it a pure function of the Graph's true state -> the true state.* Corollaries, each of which becomes a rule or an acceptance line rather than a mechanic: (1) a trail is never drawn where the Graph has no descriptor, and a consequence-channel descriptor with sev >= 1 is never left undrawn on screen at the current zoom step (FT-3, FT-19); (2) the thickest point of every trail is its source, so following the gradient always ends at the failing fitting, seam, opening or rib (FT-3); (3) a trail stays on a floor, wall face, seam, opening frame or fitting, never on a machine body sprite, a gauge or a crewmate (FT-24); (4) the only way to remove a trail is to change the Graph (valve, patch, breaker, cut, warmth, time); no verb, toggle, setting, sanity stage or hallucination removes one (FT-2); (5) a trail is seen only by spending light, and in the dark the hiss, the cold and the draught still tell (FT-26). *Worked application:* "add a soft cyan outline to a leaking pipe so players spot it at maximum zoom-out" is a marker, not a mark, and adds a world-space highlight layer the art bible rejected; **rejected**. If legibility fails at the ladder floor the fix lives in the stamp itself (the 50 % legibility gate, FT-34), never in an added layer.
63	
64	**Under hallucination the fantasy deepens rather than breaks.** Each sanity stage raises the *value* of the trail instead of eroding it. The ladder below is the table of record for the Player Fantasy; each row cites the rule that already guarantees it.
65	
66	| Sanity drift stage (concept, Visual Identity Anchor) | What lies | What the trail does | The player learns | Guaranteed by |
67	|---|---|---|---|---|
68	| 1. Instruments disagree | gauge needle, inspect card | Unchanged; the gauge's physical witness (the Graph's LS-22 table, `LSG:205`) is still drawn when lit | "check the pipe, not the needle" | the consequence-channel list (`LSG:168`); In-World Instruments pairs with this system as the truth check (provisional, `IDX:39`) |
69	| 2. The light lies (the cone looks longer, phantom shadows) | the Filter's colour pass over the perceived cone | Trails are lit only by the **true** reveal radius (Lighting, a truth channel per the kernel's non-claim, `KERN:44`); beyond it the floor stays dark even where the cone *seems* to reach | "if the frost isn't lit, my light isn't there": the trail falsifies the light lie | FT-26; `PIPE:206` mask (provisional on Lighting) |
70	| 3. Loop hues bleed violet at pipe silhouettes (`ART:232`, `ART:238`) | pipe edges | The trail keeps its loop hue and contrast; violet on a pipe beside an unviolet frost fan is itself a tell | "the pipe is wrong, the frost is right" | the Filter is colour-only and truth-masked (`PIPE:206`); FT-2, FT-22 |
71	| Class (b), false system state | machine sprite whole or broken, gauge | The mark at the fitting is unchanged (ET-5) | "the floor outranks the machine" | FT-24 (anchored at the fitting, never on the body) |
72	| Class (a), phantom entity | a monster that is not there | A phantom tears nothing: it leaves no descriptor, so no mark. A **real** hidden entity that ruptures the hull leaves an ordinary BREACH or LEAK descriptor, drawn like any breach. Caveat in the Dependencies and Open Questions: a GOUGE on a non-hull subject surfaces only as the corruptible WORN descriptor, so "never the trail" is guaranteed for the hull, not yet for ducts and cables | "did it leave a mark?" is a check that costs a walk and light | FT-31; the routed Graph/Horror gap |
73	| Class (c), crewmate as horror | crewmate sprite | Not applicable to trails; the crewmate's lamp is the human channel (Lighting, Controller). Stated so this GDD does not reach for it | none | none (out of scope) |
74	| Class (d), phantom salvage | crate contents | A module's own fitting on a derelict may carry a dried trail from its authored dead fault: a cheap field read ("this one arced") that exists only where Derelict Authoring placed a dead fault | a candidate field check, never a guarantee | `LSG:226`; opportunity routed to Salvage and Derelict Authoring |
75	
76	**Two non-negotiables (the guarantee half of the framing).** *The Filter may neither remove, alter nor add a trail* (`LSG:168`): there is no phantom trail, because a false trail would make the floor itself lie and no lie would then be falsifiable by the physical world, the one failure Pillar 4 forbids. And *this system is never a hallucination surface and has no per-player variant*: two crewmates looking at the same floor see the same marks, so co-op chatter moves from "is that scrubber green on your screen?" to "look at the floor" (the Fellowship contribution; the equal-extent promise depends on a routed Graph request, FT-33). **Cost of checking** (Pillar 4: "costs time, risk or trust"): reading a trail is never free. It costs light, a walk to where the lamp can reach, and time. The system must not reduce that cost with highlights, zoom-revealed hints or added dark-visible marks. **The one exception, stated honestly:** the emissive layer of a live scorch, arc or ember edge (FT-26, FT-27) is visible in the dark. That visibility is *paid for in Attention exposure*, not given free: the derived FAULT_GLOW emitter counts toward the web's exposure (Emitter State EM-17), so a player who walks toward a visible arc in a dark room is spending exposure to read it; the overlay itself lights nothing and exposes nothing. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* **The exposure price starts at sev 3, and that is deliberate:** the sev 1-2 `7 OVERLOAD` and `3 OVERHEAT` rims are emissive overlays with no light request (`sev_min` 3, V/A.6), so they are visible in the dark at no exposure cost. The re-review put this as a pillar tension (the early-warning read is free while Pillar 3 says emission is exposure); the rulings sheet's G2 takes the creative-director's stated lean, option (c): the sev 1-2 pre-stage tell is the fairness guarantee (P2), so it stays free to read, and the Pillar 3 trade begins where the emitter does, at sev 3 (Open Questions 6g). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text said nothing is dark-visible, which emissive faults contradict.)*
77	
78	**Known gap, closed by user ruling (Open Questions 6a): "follow the mark to the wound" now holds for a coolant leak at every temperature.** A `1 LEAK/COOLANT` descriptor in a COMFORT room (where the home ship spends most of its time) still draws the local frost fan stamp and the drip, and the frost reach there is 0 (D.3); it now also draws a **coolant wet run**: a static, dark, parallel-edged streak with a 2 px Coolant Ice edge, laid along the same chain from the fan out to the extent the trail's age has reached, its width stepping down 8 / 6 / 4 / 2 px with distance from the source (D.2d, FT-11). Following the thickening run ends at the fitting at COMFORT as following the fan does in FROST. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): Option A, a temperature-independent coolant wet run with its own thickness gradient;** Option B ("gradient guaranteed in FROST and colder only") is not adopted. AC-26c asserts it. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
79	
80	**Reference techniques, taken precisely.**
81	
82	| Reference | Adopt (exact technique) | Reject (exact technique) |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| Pandorum | the chest lamp as the only reader of a dark ship; the ship as the reliable narrator | none |
85	| Barotrauma | hull damage drawn where it is, as cracks on the wall you go to with a tool; a leak is a medium you see | the Status Monitor ship-overview screen; any per-room damage percentage |
86	| Dead Space (2008) | information lives on the world, not a HUD | the floor **locator line** pointing at the objective: a trail points to a source only because physics put it there, never to a goal |
87	| Return of the Obra Dinn | reconstructing cause from residue with no hint system (the verdict grammar, ET-4) | the confirmation ping when a deduction is right: no "correct" feedback |
88	| Project Zomboid | the room as a record; the base degrades on its own clock and noticing is competence | numeric condition readouts in context menus |
89	| Batman: Arkham, Witcher senses, any detective vision | none | any highlight, x-ray or scan mode that reveals trails or tints failing pipes: it turns reading into a button press and destroys "light is a decision" |
90	| Oxygen Not Included | gas and liquid as visible media, propagation shown in the medium | gas, temperature and power **overlays** (forbidden by `LSG:1003`) |
91	| Alien: Isolation | hissing pipes and leaking steam as the atmosphere of failure; checking costs you | **ambient decorative steam vents** that mean nothing: every mist here is a descriptor (no orphan trail, `ART:669`) |
92	| The Long Dark | cold read from the world before any number | **screen-space frost** on the view edge: body cues are Suit and HUD's, and this system draws nothing in screen space |
93	| FTL | causality between doors and air | room fire and breach **icons** (the icon layer the art bible rejected, `ART:44`-`ART:55`) |
94	| Dwarf Fortress fluids | propagation visible, not announced | per-tile simulation of the spread (the spatial gradient is presentation interpolation, `LSG:974`) |
95	
96	**Tone and language (for every later document that names a trail).** Use the art bible's five behaviour words and the Graph's names: *mist drifts; frost fan, static, crystalline; scorch, sharp, radial, blooms; puddle, glossy, flat, ember edge (a stain when dried); hairline -> crack -> bent rib*; and *drip, weep, seam, bead, fitting, elbow, collar, lagging, residue*, with *still / live* and *dull / fresh* as the two axes. Avoid "smoke", "fog", "steam" (ambient, or the rejected perception mask); "rime" for coolant (branching rime is the hidden-entity footprint's word, `ART:565`); "burn mark", "explosion", "sparks shower" (combat register); "blood", "bleed", "pool of" anything bodily (flesh is sanity's hue, red is the alarm's); "damage decal", "health crack" (stat language); "leak indicator", "warning", "alert", "HP", "damage %" (meter language); "dead/active effect", "fades out" (a fade is presentation state); and "objective", "marker", "waypoint", "hint", "highlight" (guidance-system drift). Modes are always written `id NAME/MEDIUM` as the Graph does, and the count is always "six hazard groups, eighteen descriptor ids" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: id 27 PATCH_WEEP is the eighteenth; this GDD's earlier count was seventeen)*.
97	
98	**What this GDD does not promise (anti-pillar guard rails; each traces to a pillar or anti-pillar and to the rule that enforces it).**
99	1. **No guidance system.** No marker, outline, ping, highlight, scan mode, objective line, world-space icon or arrow. A trail exists only where a descriptor exists, in the art bible's vocabulary (P1 design test; FT-3, FT-4).
100	2. **No meter, readout or alarm.** No numeric leak rate, hp tint, health bar, ship-status, schematic or minimap; never the alarm colour; `alarm_eligible` constrains this system only negatively (never first). UI Requirements: none; the three diegetic surfaces are the Graph's, and this system adds no surface (`LSG:1003`; FT-4).
101	3. **No lie on the floor.** No phantom trail, no "perceived" variant, no per-player trail, no sanity-driven change to any trail property (P4; FT-2).
102	4. **No repair reward.** No "fixed!" sparkle, completion ping, fade-out flourish or satisfaction effect. After a repair, a cap or a cut the descriptor is gone and the stamp is gone the next frame; the reward is the absence. **A patch leaves a small weep, not a clean floor:** the Graph clears the LEAK mode at the patch and a patched subject (`hp_cap` below `HP_FULL`, `hp` below `HP_OK`) then carries the descriptor-only id `27 PATCH_WEEP` instead of WORN (consequence channel, sev 1: LS-11, LS-14), so the fan, the wet run and the drip are gone the next frame and one small static s mark stays at the fitting for as long as the patch holds. The three-way contrast is the grammar: **a closed valve leaves the full mark, still; a patch leaves a small weep, static; a cap or a cut leaves nothing.** The weep is the patch's own truth (it can fail), never a reward: no sparkle, no completion cue (FT-32). (`LSG:50` "no completion ping"; FT-1.) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
103	5. **No combat feedback.** No hit-flash, damage number, impact decal for tool use against horrors, or "blood". A horror's own marks are web grammar, owned by Horror Entities (anti-pillar "not a combat game"; FT-4, FT-31).
104	6. **No light, and no readability in the dark.** A trail is a lit mark; it casts no light; the emissive layer on scorch, arc and ember is the only glow and it lights nothing; the sev 1-2 OVERLOAD and OVERHEAT rims are dark-visible without an exposure cost, a stated pillar trade (Open Questions 6g) (P3; FT-26, FT-27). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* Whether a fault's glow counts toward the web's exposure is decided by Emitter State's EM-17 (designed): the derived FAULT_GLOW emitter counts as exposure, the overlay does not.
105	7. **No cleaning, painting or decorating.** No verb, tool or setting erases or places a trail; welding is functional. Derelict authoring may not place loop-vocabulary decals that are not Graph faults (dead faults are Graph faults, `LSG:226`) (anti-pillar "not a freeform builder"; FT-3).
106	8. **No story beats.** Trails are not authored narrative props; the verdict grammar emerges from authored Graph faults, never from scripted sequences (anti-pillar "no authored story").
107	9. **No progression or score.** No count of trails fixed and no repair achievement surfaced by this system (anti-pillar "no win state"; `LSG:52`).
108	10. **Accessibility never removes truth.** Reduced motion holds moving media on a frame (direction and density kept); reduce flashing holds arcs as a steady glow; neither hides a trail (`PIPE:847`; FT-28, FT-29).
109	
110	## Detailed Design
