110	## Detailed Design
111	
112	### Core Rules
113	
114	*Every rule below describes what the player sees and when; node classes appear only in the Engine notes (the closing sub-heading of Visual/Audio Requirements) and the budget table (D.9), tagged as ADR candidates; the registry facts this system introduces are handed to the registry stage in `registry-candidates.yaml`, not duplicated here. Rule ids are `FT-n`; formulas are `D.n` in the Formulas section and are named, never restated, here; knobs are UPPER_SNAKE in Tuning Knobs. The system registers **no block, no step hook and no command**: the words "hook", "block" and "command" appear below only in sentences that say so. Registry constants are cited by their registered name and value (`TICK_RATE` 60, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10, `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, `TILE_PX` 48, `V_WALK` 2 and `V_RUN` 3 px per tick); Graph-owned constants (`LEAK_HP`, `BREACH_HP`, `ALARM_SEV_MIN`, `A_HOLE_MAX`, `SEV_STEP`, `OPEN_END_RATE_PM`, `FREEZE_WARN_MC` and kin) are registered with source the Graph GDD (2026-10-27) and are cited by registered name and value; they are not this system's to change. A value this system needs from an undesigned neighbour or a Graph field the Graph has not defined is tagged **PROVISIONAL** with its owner; a value this system owns and no neighbour has fixed is tagged **[PLACEHOLDER: NAME]** with its registry candidate. Where the art-director or an advisor ruling changed a row of a table of record, the row was rewritten, not annotated.*
115	
116	#### 1. Identity and channel
117	
118	**FT-1 Statelessness.** Every visual property of every trail element is a pure function of `read_view` fields (`failures()`, `compartment()`, `node()` and `edge()`), Layout geometry and `present_time` (animation phase only). The system owns no timer, no fade, no grow counter, no smoothing accumulator, no "last seen" flag, no spawn-time stamp and no `Tween`; the only members that persist across a Graph step are pooled scene-node references, the per-step cache of the last `read_view` poll (which is a copy of truth and not state) and **the diagnostic latch set `diag_latch` (a set of `(log_id, subject_id)` pairs, FT-41), which no draw, reconcile or selection path may read** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the logging flags were previously outlawed by the statelessness lint they also needed)*. The test: the whole trail set can be rebuilt bit-identically from one `ALL` notification and `present_time`. Control-manifest lint line: "this system has no block, no hook, no command, no light node, no `true_value()` call, and no member that survives a Graph step except pooled node references, the last poll and `diag_latch`." *Why:* the Pipeline's PR-8 rejects exactly a presentation-owned fade countdown on a trail: the moment a trail's visibility depends on presentation state it is no longer the truth channel every hallucination is checked against (`PIPE:198`; P1, P4).
119	
120	**FT-2 Truth channel.** Every node this system creates carries the TRUTH_PX grade of the Filter's PerceptionTag (registry: `perception_tag`). It reads `SIM` only, never `PERCEPTION_OUT`; it never calls `true_value()` (the Perception Filter is the only non-diagnostic caller); it has no "perceived" variant and no per-player trail. The Perception Filter may neither remove, alter nor add a trail, and this system's pixels are bit-identical with the Filter pass on or off. It works with either mask route the Filter chooses (a second viewport silhouette or per-element decomposition) and does nothing different when the mask is unavailable: in that case the Filter disables its own pass (`PIPE:735`). No sanity stage, setting, verb or hallucination class changes any trail property. *Why:* P4 "no lie is unfalsifiable"; the closed consequence-channel list (`LSG:168`); PR-10 (`PIPE:206`).
121	
122	**FT-3 Descriptor-only drawing; one trail per source.** Every drawn element sits at a descriptor's anchor on a floor, wall face, seam, opening frame or fitting. No descriptor, no element. A source (one descriptor, keyed by the identity tuple `(subject_kind, subject_id, mode, medium, anchor)`) produces **one continuous trail, thickest at the source and never appearing at a node without upstream evidence on the connecting edge**. Two descriptors with different `mode` **or different `medium`** on one anchor draw as two trails in descriptor order (ascending `subject_id`, then `mode`, then `medium`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the tuple omitted `medium`, so a `26 SEAL_STRAIN` GAS and HEAT pair on one hatch would have merged into one trail)*. No orphan trail can occur: ambient decorative mist, steam or decals that are not Graph faults are not drawn by this system and Derelict Authoring may not place them. *Why:* "an orphan trail cannot occur" (`LSG:970`-`LSG:977`; `ART:669`; P1).
123	
124	**FT-4 What this system never draws.** No meter, schematic, minimap, loop summary, numeric leak rate, health bar, damage number, hit flash, icon layer, beacon or alarm colour; nothing on a crewmate (Suit and HUD own body cues); nothing on a machine body sprite, gauge or inspect card (the module-body channel, FT-24); no web-grammar footprint (Horror Entities); no sound, and no gating on sound (Adaptive Audio leads, `IDX:41`); nothing that shows or hides Attention (P3). *Why:* `LSG:1003`; `ART:44`-`ART:55`; the anti-pillars.
125	
126	#### 2. Signal-to-visual contract
127	
128	**FT-5 Signal roles.** The three descriptor fields each drive one visual property, as the Graph documents them: `sev` selects the stamp size and the behaviour band; `intensity_pm` selects **density** (frame count, drip cadence, mist coverage as an ordered dither of 2x2-px cells, never partial alpha); the trail's **age** selects **extent** and **accumulation** (frost reach, scorch darkening, dullness): extent and accumulation read `grow_steps` and dullness reads `mode_steps`, the two per-mode age fields the Graph adopted as GA-T (LS-14; FT-8, FT-30); the Graph's `since_steps` counts from the first sev >= 1 descriptor or from `fail_since_step`, which is not the age of the current trail (the review finding behind GA-T), and is read only for the non-dominant seam weep, whose onset it counts truly (FT-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: GA-T is adopted in LS-14)*. A sev 3+ accent at the anchor (a wet collar, a heavy frost collar, a deep scorch pit) is drawn regardless of flow, so a pipe at hp 3999 with a trickle reads "badly damaged, barely flowing" and not "big leak" (exception: a gas leak at zero flow has no pixels at all, FT-18). Because `intensity_pm` is bucketed to 100 permille by the Graph, a density change always coincides with an `F/` key (D.4). *Why:* `LSG:158`-`LSG:159` document these roles; the fairness gate counts `sev` (`LSG:144`), so size tracks the Graph-guaranteed tell (P2).
129	
130	**FT-6 Size ladder.** `trail_size` (D.1): **s (48 base px) at sev 1-2, m (96) at sev 3, l (144) at sev 4**; sev 0 draws nothing. Inside s there are two sub-tiers, *trace* (sev 1) and *full* (sev 2), so a sev 1 -> 2 step is still visible without a fourth size. For the integrity behaviour the sizes are the art bible's progression: s = **hairline**, m = **crack**, l = **bent rib or hole** (sev 4 = `A_hole` >= 32, `LSG:365`). Size is never produced by scaling a sprite (FT-22); it is a different drawing at the same pixel density. Size is a function of `sev` only (the single exception is the PUDDLE descriptor, which the Graph states at `sev` 1 but whose size follows its volume tier, D.2c), so a size change always coincides with an `F/` or `N/` key and needs no polling. **The sev-0 seam exception is retired** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the Graph now states the seam weep as a `SEAM` descriptor, mode `1 LEAK`, `medium` GAS, `sev` 1 while `A_seam` > 0 (`LSG:170`), so a physically leaking weld seam draws at s-*trace* by the ordinary size table and no special case remains in D.1, D.2 or AC-11. The s/m/l semantics are **defined by this GDD** because the art bible names "the three sizes of 3.3 and 6.3" (`ART:1043`) and neither section defines them; the art-director ratified them with the trace/full amendment. Within one trail the chain tapers: stamp ordinal i from the source uses size index `max(1, size_idx - floor(i / TAPER_STAMPS))` (D.1; integer division), where `TAPER_STAMPS` **[PLACEHOLDER: `TAPER_STAMPS`]** (default 1) is the number of run stamps laid per size tier before the chain steps down one tier, so a larger knob tapers *slower*; the source is the thickest point. *Why:* m first appears at sev 3, which is `ALARM_SEV_MIN` 3 (`LSG:901`, Graph GDD), so the physical channel visibly escalates at or before the alarm ("alarm never first", LS-13 `LSG:144`, R17; P2); large stamps stay rare, which is the draw budget (`PIPE:616`).
131	
132	**FT-7 Which size cells can be reached (finding, no new rule).** By the Graph's D.4 (`LSG:365`; worked example `LSG:381`, which gives hp 5000 -> sev 2 and a patched hp 6000 -> sev 1) a subject at `hp` just below `LEAK_HP` 4000 (`LSG:127`, Graph GDD) is sev 3 (`SEV_STEP` 1500); SEVERED is forced `sev = max(sev, 3)` (`LSG:367`, `LSG:240`). So a **live `1 LEAK` descriptor (GAS, COOLANT or FUEL), a `2 SHORT` and a forced `8 SEVERED` are always sev >= 3 at birth**: they draw at m or l and never at s. The s cells are reached only by pre-stage and ambient descriptors: `7 OVERLOAD` (sev 1-2), the `4 FREEZE` pre-stage (sev 1), the `5 BREACH` pre-stage hairline (sev 1-2, mode-5 STRUCT, confirmed by the Graph, `LSG:170`; pillar-critical for Pillar 2, see FT-32), `3 OVERHEAT`'s HOT shimmer (sev 2), `20 ATMO_COLD` (sev 2), `26 SEAL_STRAIN` (sev 1), the **seam weep** (`1 LEAK/GAS` on a SEAM, sev 1: the s-mist *trace* cell), `27 PATCH_WEEP` (sev 1 only: the s-*trace* cell of its medium's row, no new asset; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review*) and, by volume tier rather than by `sev`, a small `25 PUDDLE` (s-puddle, D.2c). **Consequence for the asset list:** author s-frost, s-scorch, s-hairline and s-strain **and s-mist (trace and full) and s-puddle** for the MVP (the earlier deferral waited on the Graph stating the seam-weep severity, which it now does). A live node `1 LEAK` (GAS, COOLANT or FUEL) is still always sev >= 3 at birth, so s-mist is reached only by the seam weep. *Why:* the pre-stage descriptors are the Graph's fairness tell (`LSG:127`); their trails are the s hairlines the player must learn to read. A wearing LEAK's own pre-stage is the WORN descriptor, which is module-body and draws nothing here (FT-32); a *patched* subject's pre-stage is `27 PATCH_WEEP`, which does. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
133	
134	**FT-8 Extent is a pure function, bounded twice.** The drawn length of a trail along its edge (D.2 `trail_extent`) is the **minimum of three things, never less than `MIN_EXTENT_PX`** (an m or l head stamp is revealed by D.10 like every other stamp, so at `grow_steps` 0 a sev 4 head shows 48 of its 144 px, threshold 42 of 127, and a sev 3 head 48 of 96, threshold 63; this is the intended "it begins" read and not an undrawn source): the physical edge length; the **age bound** `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev] x grow_steps` (clamped by `SINCE_CLAMP`), where **`grow_steps` is the trail's own age: the steps since the descriptor entered its current mode or last changed `sev`, frozen at the isolation step while a closed valve isolates it** (both are descriptor fields the Graph derives from three persisted onset fields, `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step`, adopted as **GA-T** in LS-14, FT-30; they are not the Graph's `since_steps`, which counts from `fail_since_step` for a FAILED node or edge and from `warn_since_step` otherwise, so a LEAK that was a WORN node for half an hour would otherwise arrive fully grown, and every endogenous fault would arrive with at least the 100 fairness-gate steps already counted, which is 600 px at sev 3 and 1500 px at sev 4); and, for `4 FREEZE` only, the **temperature bound** `reach_px` (D.3 `frost_reach`; the whole edge for every other row; **for `1 LEAK/COOLANT` the temperature no longer limits the extent: it limits only how much of the run is drawn as frost, `frost_px`, D.2d**, user ruling D26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. All arithmetic is integer; the result is floored to base px. A live descriptor therefore always draws the first `MIN_EXTENT_PX` 48 [PLACEHOLDER: `MIN_EXTENT_PX`] base px of its source stamp on its first step. **A severity change restarts the age** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; resolves the "sev rise redraws hundreds of pixels of history in one frame" finding by the onset request; restart-at-source is kept as a default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), Open Questions 6c: neither the one-frame jump to the old age bound nor an `EXTENT_JUMP_MAX` cap is adopted)*: when `sev` changes, the Graph resets the mode onset (GA-T), so `grow_steps` is 0 on the new size's first frame, the new size's head stamp draws at `MIN_EXTENT_PX` and the extent regrows at the new severity's rate. The one-frame event is therefore a size swap and a restart at the source, never an old long mark inflated in one frame; a sev-4 bent rib that begins at the source and races along the rib at 150 px/s is the breach image (ET-3). 150	**FT-15 Keys wake, polls move.** A notification handler stores the key set and returns; it never reads or draws (`PIPE:190`, PR-8 rule 3). In the next render callback the system (1) re-reads `failures()` and `compartment()` (and, for the provisional rows of FT-30, `node()` and `edge()`, whose continuous `flow` and machine `T` dirty no key) **once per Graph step** into the per-step poll cache (the Graph runs once per `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 ticks = 0.1 s; `since_steps` dirties no key, `LSG:532`), (2) spawns, despawns and re-selects size and behaviour on `F/` and `N/`, band accents on `B/` and `C/`, and rebuilds anchors on `T` and `SEC/`, and (3) every frame reads extent, dullness and animation phase from the poll cache and `present_time`. The key-family reaction table is below. **Step detection, key union and overflow** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; these were unspecified)*: a Graph step is detected by comparing the read view's `step_no` (the counter `since_steps` is defined against, LS-14) with the `step_no` stored in the poll cache; the poll runs on a difference and on no other condition. Notifications arrive once per tick (P5) and the render callback may run less often than the kernel ticks (30 Hz rendering, a hitch), so the handler **unions** every key set received since the last callback (a set, no duplicates, order irrelevant: a spawn-then-despawn pair within the union is resolved by the poll, which is the truth); if the union grows past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, or an `ALL` is among the notifications, the callback treats the union as `ALL` (FT-16). *Why:* LS-20 (`LSG:201`) says keys wake discrete presentation only; PR-8 rule 3 and the kernel's CR-10.

167	**FT-18 A gas leak at zero flow is empty by design.** `1 LEAK/GAS` (and `8 SEVERED/GAS`) at `intensity_pm` 0 draws **zero pixels**: "O2 failure leaves no trail (mist evaporates), read from absence" (`ART:697`), and no residue accent exists for GAS (a stain would suggest a false O2 history on a derelict). A sev-3 trickle therefore reads "wide, sparse plume". This GDD **reads the Graph's lint** (`LSG:1110`, which scans for a consumer that "suppresses a consequence-channel descriptor whose sev >= 1 from its physical channel") as: *no consequence-channel descriptor with `medium` != NONE and sev >= 1 may be hidden from its physical channel while it has flow; an empty STILL GAS plume is not suppression, because the physical flow is zero.* The reading is this GDD's, not the Graph's, and is listed in Open Questions as routed to the Graph owner (non-blocking). **`27 PATCH_WEEP` on a GAS subject (a patched duct or O2 tank) is the second drawn-and-empty case** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2; creative-director ruling on the specialist disagreement)*: it draws zero pixels, because the Graph states that a PATCH_WEEP carries no flow (LS-11) and a dry-seam residue is rejected (it would suggest a false O2 history on a derelict, the reason this rule exists, and it contradicts "read from absence"). The consequence-channel tell is the **HISS** that Adaptive Audio plays at the descriptor's anchor (FT-35), and it is not suppressed, so R17 (no consumer may suppress a consequence-channel descriptor's acoustic or physical channel) is met acoustically. Recorded as the explicit FT-18 note: the Graph owner is asked to confirm that reading (Open Questions 43); this system never draws a GAS weep mark. *Why:* the verdict grammar (P5); `ART:697`.
168	
169	**FT-19 Never cull an on-screen consequence-channel element.** Every descriptor with `medium` != NONE and sev >= 1 **whose trail's bounding box lies inside or crosses the camera field at the current ladder step k** has its stamps drawn that frame (subject to FT-18). The test is geometric and is made on the **polyline bounding box padded by one head cell** (the `STAMP_PX` of the trail's head size, 48, 96 or 144 px) intersected with the field, **not on the anchor point** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: an anchor-point test let a trail whose source sits off-screen but whose body crosses the view pop in as the source scrolled on, which is the suppression this rule forbids)*. Cost pressure is relieved first by reducers that change no pixel (FT-41), then by degrading moving media, in this order: frame count, then density, then `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` halving, then far-from-beam frame hold; **never stamps**. Not drawing is permitted only for trails whose padded bounding box lies wholly outside the field (re-evaluated at every k, so a zoom-out reveals every trail), dormant sections (they emit no descriptors, `LSG:822`) and sev 0. Distance culling and darkness culling are forbidden: they are exactly the suppression the Graph's lint scans for (`LSG:1110`). *Why:* P1 via `LSG:144` R17 (no consumer may suppress a consequence-channel descriptor's physical channel).
170	
171	**FT-20 Pure variation.** Stamp variant, drip phase offset and fan flip come from `rng_derive(world_seed, "trail.vis", (subject_id << 20) | stamp_index)` (D.6), the pure hash the kernel defines (`KERN:470`, D.10); the kernel's H9 restricts *simulation* from wall-clock and global randomness, and a presentation caller of a pure hash violates nothing. `world_seed` is read as exposed through **the kernel's read view of `kernel.clock`** (`KERN:477`, `KERN:844`; CR-12 makes every `SIM` block readable by presentation; the confirmation that `kernel.clock` is registered class `SIM` is routed to the kernel owner, non-blocking). If that read is not available, the fallback `TRAIL_VIS_SEED_FALLBACK` 0 [PLACEHOLDER] is identical on every client and after every restore, only less varied. Engine global random functions and any random-number-generator instance are forbidden in this system (lint). *Why:* two crewmates must see the same frost fan (P1); a restore redraws the same trail (`LSG:829`).
172

The bit pattern `0x8000000000000000` (the signed value -2^63) and `-1` (all ones) are both legal hash outputs and both mask to non-negative values. Here the counter argument is a **key** (subject and stamp), not a draw index: this system has no block, so no counter ever advances and no draw order exists.

**Output Range:** 0 to the equalisation amount divided by the degree; it never overshoots (the second term is the amount that would exactly equalise two finite volumes, or everything the room holds against vacuum) and it never goes negative (magnitude with direction); the sign of the flux is always the sign of the true gradient `g`, even when both rooms read the same floored dkPa *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. It is 0 when `A_m` = 0, when `g` = 0, and — the truncation bias TD required this document to state — whenever `G_OPEN × A × ΔP < 1`: **equalisation stalls within `⌈1/k⌉` mGU** of the exact balance, which for a pinhole (`A` = 1, `V` = 20) is 10,000 mGU = 0.5 dkPa in that room and for a door is 156 mGU. This is expected behaviour, not a defect: the residual is below the 10 dkPa dirty-key quantum and below anything a gauge or a lung can register. Maximum for a door at full vacuum: `2 × 64 × 1000` = 128,000 mGU/step (a 20-tile room empties through an open hatch in about 160 steps = 16 s; LOW band in 5.6 s — the "chaos" end of the scale, Section C LS-7). The model is linear and unchoked: a vent through a hole slows as the pressure falls, which is the readable behaviour (the hiss fades as the room dies) and the reason no table or square-root law is needed.
**Example:** room a (`V_a` = 20, `P_a` = 1000, `n_tot` = 20,000,000, `n_o2` = 4,200,000, `deg_a` = 2) to room b (`V_b` = 40, `P_b` = 400, `deg_b` = 3) through a door `A` = 64: `g` = 20,000,000 × 40 − 16,000,000 × 20 = 480,000,000 (exact `ΔP` 600); first term `2 × 64,000 × 480,000,000 / (20 × 40 × 1000 × 1000)` = 76,800; second term `480,000,000 / (60 × 3)` = 2,666,666; `Δn` = 76,800; `Δn_o2` = `⌊76,800 × 4,200,000 / 20,000,000⌋` = 16,128; `Δn_inert` = 60,672. After the step `n_a` = 19,923,200 → `P_a` = `⌊19,923,200 / 20,000⌋` = 996; `n_b` = 16,000,000 + 76,800 → `P_b` = `⌊16,076,800 / 40,000⌋` = 401. Pinhole to vacuum from the same room: `Δn` = `min(⌊2 × 1,000 × 20,000,000 / (20 × 1000 × 1000)⌋, ⌊20,000,000 / 2⌋)` = 2,000 mGU/step, `k` = 0.0001 per step.

605	### D.7 `trail_reconcile_cost`
606	
607	The `trail_reconcile_cost` formula is defined as:
608	
609	keyed step: `cost_us = n_poll x C_POLL_US + n_F x C_SPAWN_US + n_BC x C_BAND_US + n_stamp_changed x C_STAMP_US` ; `ALL`: `cost_all_us = n_desc x C_DESC_US + n_stamps x C_STAMP_US + n_pool_ops x C_POOL_US` ; check: `cost_all_us <= TRAIL_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS x 1000` (a logging threshold, never a cut-off)
610	
611	The key counts come from the Graph's `dirty_key_budget` (`LSG:532`, cited by registry name, never restated) and are bounded by `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; above that the kernel collapses the notification to `ALL` (`KERN:466`). The unit costs are placeholders pending spike S5; this is a consumer-side cost model, and the Graph's own budget is not this system's.
612	
613	**Variables:**
614	
615	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
616	|---|---|---|---|---|
617	| `n_F`, `n_BC` | int | 0-256 | per-family counts of `dirty_key_budget` (`F/` keys; `B/` + `C/` keys) | Keys this step |
618	| `n_poll`, `n_desc` | int | 0 - `N_DESC_DESIGN_MAX` | `failures()` size | Descriptors polled (once per Graph step) or re-read (`ALL`) |
619	| `n_stamps`, `n_stamp_changed` | int | 0 - `TRAIL_MAX_STAMPS` | D.1, D.2 | Stamps in the pool; stamps changed this step |
620	| `n_pool_ops` | int | 0-256 | pool | Pool acquire and release operations |
621	| `C_POLL_US`, `C_SPAWN_US`, `C_BAND_US`, `C_STAMP_US`, `C_DESC_US`, `C_POOL_US`, `C_FIELD_US`, `C_FRAME_US` | int us | 2 / 30 / 10 / 3 / 15 / 5 / 1 / 4 **[PLACEHOLDER: unit costs]** | spike S5 | Unit costs (the last two price a pan frame and an animation flip, below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
622	| `N_DESC_DESIGN_MAX` | int | 32-128 (default 64) **[PLACEHOLDER: `N_DESC_DESIGN_MAX`]** | tuning | Design maximum of live descriptors |
623	| `TRAIL_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS` | float ms | 0.5-6 (default 4) **[PLACEHOLDER: `TRAIL_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS`]** | tuning | Logging threshold for an in-play `ALL` (a diff); `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is the kernel's, not this system's *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
624	| `TRAIL_RESTORE_BUDGET_MS` | float ms | 4-16 (default 8) **[PLACEHOLDER: `TRAIL_RESTORE_BUDGET_MS`]** | tuning | Logging threshold for a restore or instantiation `ALL` (a full rebuild) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

The unit cost `C_STAMP_US` 3 is the best case: the technical-artist's own estimate is about 6 writes per stamp, which with `C_STAMP_US` 6 gives 5,661 us and 5,418 us for the last two. **Two thresholds, not one** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the single 2 ms threshold fired on every legal worst-case world, and a gameplay-time `ALL` was costed as a full rebuild)*: a **restore or instantiation `ALL`** is a full rebuild, once, and is logged above `TRAIL_RESTORE_BUDGET_MS` 8 **[PLACEHOLDER]** (the modelled worst is 5.7 ms; the measured pass thresholds of spike S5 are the same 8 ms and 12 ms); an **in-play `ALL`** (a cascade above `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 while the game runs) is modelled as a **diff against the pool**, not a rebuild: `cost_all_play_us = n_desc x C_DESC_US + n_stamp_changed x C_STAMP_US + n_pool_ops x C_POOL_US`, with `n_stamp_changed` at most the stamps of the newly failed descriptors (221 at `fx_mvp_worst`, 294 at `fx_design_max`), which gives 2,358 us and 2,592 us at `C_STAMP_US` 3 and 3,021 us and 3,474 us at 6, logged above `TRAIL_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS` 4 **[PLACEHOLDER]** (raised from 2). Both are logging thresholds and never cut anything (FT-16, FT-19). Both estimates are `[UNV]` until measured; the **spike S5 pass thresholds** are [PLACEHOLDER] measured `ALL` <= 8 ms at `fx_mvp_worst` and <= 12 ms at `fx_design_max` on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (delegated ruling R12; pending spike measurement; half a 60 Hz frame and three quarters of one at RM-DESKTOP's 16.6 ms ceiling; the Deck lines are not claimed to hold until S5 measures them).
627	**Example:** steady, 17 descriptors and 3 `F/` keys: 17 x 2 + 3 x 30 = **124 us**. MVP worst cascade, 63 descriptors polled, 12 `F/`, 10 `B/` or `C/`, 60 stamps changed: 63 x 2 + 12 x 30 + 10 x 10 + 60 x 3 = **766 us** (640 us without the poll term; 946 us with `C_STAMP_US` 6). `ALL` after a restore, 17 descriptors, 102 stamps, 40 pool ops: 17 x 15 + 102 x 3 + 40 x 5 = 255 + 306 + 200 = **761 us** = 0.76 ms <= 2 ms.
628	
629	**Frame classes and the p99 target** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the 0.25 ms p99 was stated per render frame, but a keyed cascade costs 640 us by this very model)*. A Graph step is one tick in six, so at 60 Hz one render frame in six is a **step frame** (the frame that polls and applies keys) and five are **idle frames**; a p99 over all frames therefore lands on step frames. **Four frame classes, four budgets** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: only idle and step frames were budgeted, but a walking player makes almost every frame a pan frame and every fifth an animation-flip frame; the step budget's "2x headroom" was false (1.0 ms against a modelled 0.64 ms that also omitted the poll term, 0.77 ms with it, 0.95 ms at `C_STAMP_US` 6))*: a frame is classed by the most expensive event it carries. **Idle** (no step, no key, no frame-index change, no camera-field change): `TRAIL_FRAME_MS_P99` 0.25 ms (FT-41 rule 1: they write nothing, so the cost is scheduler overhead only). **Pan** (the camera field moved; the in-field test of FT-19 is re-evaluated for every trail): `cost_pan_us = n_trails x C_FIELD_US + n_enter_leave x C_SPAWN_US`, with `C_FIELD_US` 1 **[PLACEHOLDER]**, `n_trails` at most `N_DESC_DESIGN_MAX` 64 and `n_enter_leave` at most 8 per frame, which is 304 us, budget `TRAIL_PAN_FRAME_MS_P99` 0.5 ms **[PLACEHOLDER]**. **Animation flip** (the stepped-strip frame index changed, one render frame in five at 12 fps; no step, no key): `cost_anim_us = n_moving x C_FRAME_US`, with `C_FRAME_US` 4 **[PLACEHOLDER]** and `n_moving` at most 128 moving-media sprites, which is 512 us, budget `TRAIL_ANIM_FRAME_MS_P99` 0.75 ms **[PLACEHOLDER]** if the index is written to scene nodes; if spike S2 shows the frame index can be shader-driven from `present_time` (a shared uniform, V/A.13), an animation flip writes nothing and joins the idle class at 0.25 ms (S2 decides). **Step** (the frame that polls and applies keys, excluding `ALL`): `TRAIL_STEP_FRAME_MS_P99` **1.5 ms [PLACEHOLDER]** (raised from 1.0: 1.5 ms is 1.96 times the modelled 0.766 ms with the poll term and 1.6 times the 0.946 ms of the technical-artist's own unit cost, so the headroom is about twice). The cost of a step frame is O(trails currently growing, keyed or changed, plus the poll), not O(stamps). The profiling criterion measures a walking player so all four classes occur in their real mix (AC-83, AC-174, AC-183).

631	### D.8 `anim_frame`
632	
633	The `anim_frame` formula is defined as:
634	
635	`frame = 0 if reduced_motion else (floor(present_time x TRAIL_ANIM_FPS) + phase_offset) mod N_FRAMES[medium]` ; `drip_phase`, mist, debris, dust and shimmer use this form; the growth tip uses `tip_frame = floor(trail_extent_px / STAMP_STRIDE_PX) mod 3` (a function of extent, not of time)
636	
637	`present_time` is the one float in this system: the Pipeline's render-rate clock (PR-9), frozen while the kernel is PAUSED, used for animation phase only, never hashed and never read by the Graph. Using a float here is allowed because the result selects a sprite frame and cannot affect any simulation state or replicated value; a stepped (10-12 Hz) result is not required to be bit-identical between clients, only equal in kind (FT-28's hold frame is).
638	
639	**Variables:**
640	
641	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
642	|---|---|---|---|---|
643	| `present_time` | float s | >= 0, frozen while PAUSED | Pipeline PR-9 | The only animation clock; never wall-clock, never the tick counter (PR-8 rule 6) |
644	| `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` | int | 6-24 (default 12; safe 8-12) **[PLACEHOLDER: `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS`]** | tuning | Stepped media rate (the 12 fps horror-rig precedent, `PIPE:202`) |
645	| `phase_offset` | int | 0 - `N_FRAMES` - 1 | D.6 | Per-trail phase |
646	| `N_FRAMES[medium]` | int | 2-12 | asset spec | Frames per loop |
647	| `reduced_motion` | bool | - | Settings (FT-36, provisional) | Holds frame 0 (FT-28) |
648	| `STAMP_STRIDE_PX` | int px | 48 | D.1 (`STAMP_PX[1]`) | Run stride for the growth-tip frame |
649	
650	**Output Range:** `frame` in 0..`N_FRAMES` - 1; `tip_frame` in 0..2. Under reduced motion every moving medium is on frame 0, its authored hold frame (FT-28).

I'm double-checking the arithmetic across each scenario—fx_steady, fx_mvp_worst, design_max, and the variants with C_STAMP set to 6—confirming the totals all add up correctly.

Now I'm thinking through performance budgets on RM-DECK: the frame-time ceiling is 33.3 ms versus 16.6 ms on desktop, but Deck's CPU is slower, so I need to weigh that extra headroom against weaker hardware before trusting the same ms budgets. I'm also cross-checking that the restore operations staying under 8 ms makes sense as roughly half a 60Hz frame, and three-quarters for 12 ms, while noting Deck's actual target is 30 fps with its own animation tick rate that I need to reconcile against these budgets.

At 30 fps, one render frame covers two kernel ticks instead of one, so the assumption that every sixth render frame aligns with a step frame breaks down -- it's really every third render frame now. This means the frame classification scheme built for 60 fps doesn't map cleanly onto Deck's 30 fps mode, and I should check whether the GDD actually specifies 30 fps for Deck before trying to restate the frame classes for it.

173	#### 4. Look: technique, bands, pixels
174	
175	**FT-21 Static stamps and stepped frames.** Static marks (frost fan, crust and sheath, scorch, glossy streak, puddle, hairline, crack and bent rib, bowed rim, rim frost, soot wash, and any dulled form) are **stamps** from the three-size sheets. Moving media (mist drift, drip, vent debris, wind streaks, AIRFLOW dust, arc pops, shimmer) are **pooled stepped sprite frames** at `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` 12 [PLACEHOLDER] (the horror-rig precedent of 12 fps stepped, `PIPE:202`), with frame index from `present_time` (D.8), never from wall-clock or the tick counter (PR-8 rule 6). Particle systems are permitted **only** for venting at a BREACH or AIRFLOW opening, and only after a spike proves (a) per-instance positions floor to the base grid and (b) alpha is binary under nearest sampling (both unverified, HIGH risk); until then venting is stepped frames too. The "propagation frames" the art bible lists for the trail sheet are not needed and are dropped from the asset list: a growing front is a reveal threshold (FT-23), not extra drawings. *Why:* binary alpha and integer placement are exactly where particles are weakest; stepped frames satisfy both by construction (FT-22).
176	
177	**FT-22 Pixel integrity.** Nearest sampling; every item at an integer base-px position (placed by `floor`); **no per-node scale animation of any kind** (growth is stamp count, size swap and the reveal threshold of FT-23); `rotation` 0; hairlines, filaments and seams are **sprites, never runtime line draws** (PR-4 rule 10; the engine's 4.7 line-antialiasing change is moot for exactly this reason); alpha is binary (0 or 255) on every drawn sprite, including mist (a partially transparent mist is not pixel art); palette lock; minimum feature 2x2 px, except that a hairline is a **1 px Hull Grey run paired with a 1 px Void Steel shadow line (a 2 px composite, at least 4 px long)**, which the art-director ratified as a permitted 1 px element joining contour and glyph strokes (the *dried* 2 px coolant wet-run piece uses the same composite, V/A.3; *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review*), an amendment candidate to the art bible's minimum-feature checklist (routed); no single-pixel noise; no violet and no flesh hue in any trail sheet or any dulled render; the alarm colour, the glowstick light colour and human (Tungsten) light appear in no trail. *Why:* `PIPE:110`-`PIPE:123`; `ART:1088`; `ART:422`-`ART:430`.
178	
179	**FT-23 Chain, reveal by threshold, density by dither.** A trail is an **anchor cap** at the source, **run** pieces chained along the polyline, a **tip** at the leading edge, **corner** pieces where Layout turns the line, and a **terminal** piece when the extent reaches its bound. The last run piece is revealed up to the extent by comparing its flow-phase ramp channel with an integer threshold (so a frost front is ragged and a scorch front radial with no extra art), never by scaling. Density (FT-5) is a **world-anchored dither of 2x2-px cells**, never partial alpha: the pattern keys on world base-px coordinates so it does not swim with the camera, overlapped stamps agree and every client draws the same pixels. 369	## Formulas
370	
371	*Conventions. Every formula here is a pure function of Graph fields, Layout geometry and the render clock (FT-1); none has state. All arithmetic is integer, with `floor` (integer division) stated wherever pixels or counts are produced, so everything that selects what is drawn is bit-identical on every client and after every restore (the kernel's determinism rule applies to anything hashed or replicated; nothing here is hashed, but FT-2 and FT-33 make equality of the drawn set a requirement). The only float is `present_time` in D.8 (the Pipeline's render-rate clock, PR-9; presentation only, never hashed, never fed back into the Graph) and `tick_alpha` in D.2's optional smoothing. Graph formulas (D.2 hole geometry `LSG:308`, D.4 efficiency and severity `LSG:361`, D.10 `dirty_key_budget` `LSG:532`, D.11 `fairness_gate`) are **cited by name and never re-derived**; where a worked example needs a Graph value it is taken as given and labelled so. Values tagged **[PLACEHOLDER: NAME]** are this system's, have a registry candidate of that name, and are tuned in Tuning Knobs. Rule ids `FT-n` are in Detailed Design; formula ids `D.n` here (registered names: `trail_size`, `trail_extent`, `frost_reach`, `dullness`, `arc_flash_share`, `trail_budget_at_k`, `trail_reconcile_cost`; unregistered section-local names: `trail_density`, `trail_stamp_variant`, `anim_frame`, `trail_reveal`).*
372	
373	### D.1 `trail_size`
374	
375	The `trail_size` formula is defined as:
376	
377	`size_idx = 0 if sev = 0 else min(3, max(1, sev - 1))` ; `sub_tier = trace if sev <= 1 else full` (meaningful only when `size_idx` = 1; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the sev-0 seam exception is retired, FT-6, because the Graph states the seam weep at sev 1*) ; chain: `idx_i = max(1, size_idx - floor(i / TAPER_STAMPS))`, `start(0) = 0`, `start(i + 1) = start(i) + STAMP_PX[idx_i]`
378	
379	Derived: `n_cover(E)` = the smallest `n` with `start(n)` >= `E` (the stamps needed to cover an extent `E` from D.2); the chain tapers so the source is the thickest point, and a larger `TAPER_STAMPS` tapers *slower*.
380	
381	**Variables:**
382	
383	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
384	|---|---|---|---|---|
385	| `sev` | int | 0-4 | descriptor `sev` (Graph D.4, `LSG:365`) | Severity; 0 draws nothing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
386	| `size_idx` | int | {0, 1, 2, 3} | calculated | 0 none, 1 s (48 base px), 2 m (96), 3 l (144) |
387	| `sub_tier` | enum | {trace, full} | calculated | The two sub-tiers inside s: sev 1 trace, sev 2 full (FT-6) |
388	| `STAMP_PX` | int[3] | 48 / 96 / 144 | `ART:1043`, defined by FT-6 | Stamp length along the chain for `size_idx` 1 / 2 / 3 |
389	| `TAPER_STAMPS` | int | 1-3 (default 1) **[PLACEHOLDER: `TAPER_STAMPS`]** | tuning | Run stamps laid per size tier before the chain steps down one tier |
390	| `i` | int | 0 - 2^20 - 1 | calculated | Stamp ordinal from the source (0 = anchor cap) |
391	| `idx_i` | int | 1-3 | calculated | Size index of stamp `i` |
392	| `start(i)` | int px | 0-1152 | calculated | Offset of stamp `i` from the source along the polyline |
393	
394	**Output Range:** `size_idx` 0..3: sev 1 and 2 -> 1; sev 3 -> 2; sev 4 -> 3. `idx_i` never rises along the chain and never falls below 1, so no stamp is larger than the source stamp. With `TAPER_STAMPS` 1 the start offsets are: sev 4: 0, 144, 240, 288, 336, ...; sev 3: 0, 96, 144, 192, ...; sev 1-2: 0, 48, 96, ... . Not clamped further: every input is bounded by the Graph. Wall cells are 48 / 96 / 144 px wide and at most 72 px tall (FT-13); `STAMP_PX` is the along-run length.
395	**Example:** a hull plate at `hp` 1500, which the Graph's D.4 maps to sev 4 (taken as given), gives `size_idx` 3. With `TAPER_STAMPS` 1 the stamps are l (144) at 0, m (96) at 144, s (48) at 240, 288, 336 ...; `n_cover(336)` = 4 (`start(3)` = 288 < 336, `start(4)` = 336 >= 336). With `TAPER_STAMPS` 2 the same plate lays l, l, m, m, s, s ...: starts 0, 144, 288, 384, 480, 528 (a fatter, slower taper). A coolant pipe at sev 3 gives `size_idx` 2: m at 0, then s at 96, 144, 192 ....

397	### D.2 `trail_extent`
398	
399	The `trail_extent` formula is defined as:
400	
401	`age_steps = min(grow_steps, SINCE_CLAMP)` ; `age_px = GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev] x age_steps` ; `reach_px = frost_reach(T)` (D.3) when the row is `4 FREEZE`, else `edge_len_px` (**`1 LEAK/COOLANT` has no temperature term in its extent: its `reach_px` here is `edge_len_px`, and `frost_reach(T)` bounds only `frost_px`, D.2d**) ; `trail_extent_px = min(edge_len_px, max(MIN_EXTENT_PX, min(age_px, reach_px)))` ; optional render smoothing (`TRAIL_EXTENT_SMOOTH` true only): `E_disp = E(n - 1) + floor((E(n) - E(n - 1)) x alpha_pm / 1000)` with `alpha_pm = floor(tick_alpha x 1000)`, `E(n)` the value above at `grow_steps`, `E(n - 1)` the same expression at `max(0, grow_steps - 1)` with the same `sev` and `T`; otherwise `E_disp = E(n)`. **`grow_steps` is the trail's own age (FT-8, GA-T, adopted in LS-14): `max(0, (isolated_at_step if isolated_at_step > 0 else step_no) - mode_since_step)`, where the Graph restamps `mode_since_step` whenever the subject's dominant descriptor changes its `mode_key` = `(mode << 3) | sev`; the resolver reads the descriptor's `grow_steps` field and never recomputes it, except that a non-dominant descriptor takes the interim rule of FT-8 (head only; the seam weep reads `since_steps`).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* D.2 applies to the RUN class only (geometry-class table, Detailed Design section 6); `20 ATMO_COLD` and `21 ATMO_HOT` use D.2b and read no age. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the age was the Graph's `since_steps`, `sev_g` existed only for the retired seam exception, and `20 ATMO_COLD` was listed as a cold RUN row.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: the coolant leak is no longer a temperature-bounded row, Open Questions 6a, D.2d.)*
402	
403	Derived (the tell-window invariants, testable): `crossing_steps(L, sev) = ceil(L / GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev])` ; (i) `crossing_steps(288, 1) <= 288` (28.8 s, inside the 10-30 s tell ceiling of `PIPE:1081` item 15); (ii) `V_WALK` x `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` = 12 < `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[4]` <= `V_RUN` x `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` = 18; (iii) `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev]` monotone non-decreasing in `sev`; (iv) in the cryo-bay fixture (sev 3) `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[3]` x 10 <= `DRIP_FALL_PX_PER_FRAME` x `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` ("nothing moves faster than the drip", `ART:142`).
404	
405	**Variables:**
406	
407	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
408	|---|---|---|---|---|
409	| `sev` | int | 1-4 | descriptor | Severity (a change of `sev` resets `grow_steps`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
410	| `grow_steps` | int | 0 - unbounded | descriptor, **GA-T (adopted, LS-14)**: `max(0, (isolated_at_step if isolated_at_step > 0 else step_no) - mode_since_step)`, dominant descriptor only; a non-dominant descriptor takes FT-8's interim rule (`since_steps`, which the Graph counts from `built_step` for a SEAM, is read only for the seam weep) | Steps of this trail's own life: 0 at the first frame of the current mode and severity; frozen at the isolation step; for a dormant section it counts steps the section ran *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
411	| `SINCE_CLAMP` | int | 1000-65535 (default 20000) **[PLACEHOLDER: `SINCE_CLAMP`]** | tuning | Keeps `age_px` inside 32-bit shader uniforms; 20000 steps = 33 min (clamps `grow_steps` only; dullness reads `mode_steps` unclamped) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
412	| `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev]` | int px/step | sev 1: 1-4; sev 2: 2-8; sev 3: 3-7; sev 4: 13-18; default 2 / 3 / 6 / 15 **[PLACEHOLDER: `GROW_PX_PER_STEP`]** | tuning (FT-9) | Growth per Graph step (20 / 30 / 60 / 150 px/s) |
413	| `edge_len_px` | int px | 48 - `TRAIL_EDGE_MAX_PX` 1152 | Layout `anchor_geometry` (LY-23, designed) | Polyline length of the combined wall + floor run (FT-13) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
414	| `MIN_EXTENT_PX` | int px | 24-96 (default 48) **[PLACEHOLDER: `MIN_EXTENT_PX`]** | tuning | The source stamp is present from step 0 |
415	| `DRIP_FALL_PX_PER_FRAME` | int px | 4-8 (default 6) **[PLACEHOLDER: `DRIP_FALL_PX_PER_FRAME`]** | art-director (drip strip: hang 2, fall 2, land 4 frames) | Fall speed of the drip, 72 px/s at 12 fps; the benchmark for "nothing moves faster than the drip" in the cryo bay |

417	| `tick_alpha` | float | [0, 1] | Pipeline PR-9 | Interpolation fraction inside the current Graph interval; never extrapolated (`KERN:298`) |
418	| `trail_extent_px` | int px | `min(edge_len_px, 48)` - `edge_len_px` | calculated | Length to draw; floored base px |

420	**Output Range:** `min(edge_len_px, MIN_EXTENT_PX)` at `grow_steps` 0 (or when the reach bound is 0), up to `edge_len_px`. Monotone non-decreasing in `grow_steps` for a fixed `sev`; non-increasing in room `T` while the reach bound binds (a `4 FREEZE` sheath retreats as the room warms; for `1 LEAK/COOLANT` the extent does not retreat, only `frost_px` does and the wet run takes the stamps, D.2d), with no stored state *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **A severity change restarts `grow_steps` at 0** (the extent restarts at `MIN_EXTENT_PX` and regrows at the new rate: the one-frame event is a size swap, not an inflation of old history; FT-8; default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), Open Questions 6c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Isolation freezes the age bound:** while `isolated_at_step` > 0, `grow_steps` is constant, so a valve closed at `grow_steps` 50 on a sev 3 coolant leak leaves `age_px` at 6 x 50 = 300 for ever (a `4 FREEZE` sheath can still be pulled back by the temperature bound; a coolant leak's temperature pulls back only its frost part, D.2d). The frozen extent is a property of `trail_extent_px`, which exists even where FT-18 draws nothing: a `1 LEAK/GAS` plume at `intensity_pm` 0 has the same frozen `trail_extent_px` and zero visible pixels, so the GAS variant is tested on the resolver output (AC-146), not on pixels. `edge_len_px` above 1152 is a content error (lint to Layout and Derelict Authoring). `GROW_PX_PER_STEP` x `SINCE_CLAMP` is at most 18 x 65535, which fits int32.

423	#### D.2b `surface_patch_count` (ATMO_COLD, ATMO_HOT)
424	
425	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: rewritten. The earlier formula grew with `since_steps`, which the Graph states as 0 for COMPARTMENT descriptors (`LSG:170`), so room frost and soot never spread and the 21-patch example was unreachable; the first fix considered, a radius equal to the whole reach, would have popped up to 24 patches in one step at the 0 mC edge. Coverage is now a function of the room's true temperature alone, starts at 0, and is a prefix of a fixed ordering.)*
426	
427	The `surface_patch_count` formula is defined as:
428	
429	`cover_pm = 0` unless the row draws (`20 ATMO_COLD` at sev >= 2, `21 ATMO_HOT` at sev 4) ; `20 ATMO_COLD`: `cover_pm = clamp(floor((T_COOL_FROST - T) x 1000 / (T_COOL_FROST - T_FULL_COLD)), 0, 1000)` with `T_COOL_FROST` the COOL/FROST edge (0 mC) and `T_FULL_COLD` the FROST/FREEZING edge (-15000 mC, the Graph's `COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC`), both cited by position from LS-7 and never redefined here ; `21 ATMO_HOT` (sev 4): `cover_pm = clamp(floor((T - T_SCORCH) x 1000 / SOOT_RAMP_MC), 0, 1000)` with `T_SCORCH` the HOT/SCORCH edge (70000 mC, LS-7) ; candidate tiles `c_0 ... c_(N-1)` from Layout `room_surface`, sorted ascending by **`(dist_t, row, col)`** where `dist_t` is the **Manhattan distance in tiles** from the anchor tile (the **room-fixed anchor tile** of FT-11: the lowest `(row, col)` floor tile that touches an exposed hull face, else the lowest `(row, col)` floor tile of the room; a function of Layout geometry alone and never of any descriptor, so a leak appearing or clearing at constant `T` moves no patch) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* ; `m = 0` if the row does not draw, else `min(N, max(1, floor(N x cover_pm / 1000)))` ; tile `c_k` carries a patch iff `k < m` and `k mod PATCH_STRIDE = 0`, and only the first `PATCH_MAX_PER_ROOM` such tiles are kept ; `n_patches = min(PATCH_MAX_PER_ROOM, ceil(m / PATCH_STRIDE))` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

432	
433	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
434	|---|---|---|---|---|
435	| `T` | int mC | about -40000 - 90000 | `compartment(cid).T` (true value, polled once per Graph step) | Room temperature; never the perceived value (FT-2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
436	| `T_COOL_FROST`, `T_FULL_COLD`, `T_SCORCH` | int mC | 0 / -15000 / 70000 | Graph LS-7 edges, cited | Ramp knots; if LS-7 moves they move with it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
437	| `SOOT_RAMP_MC` | int mC | 5000-40000 (default 20000) **[PLACEHOLDER: `SOOT_RAMP_MC`]** | tuning | Temperature above the SCORCH edge at which the soot wash covers the whole room *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

440	| `m` | int | 0 - `N` | calculated | Length of the covered prefix of the ordering; a prefix, so the set only grows as the room cools (or heats) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
441	| `dist_t` | int tiles | 0 - room extent | calculated | Manhattan distance in tiles from the anchor tile; integer, so the order is bit-identical on every client *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

443	| `PATCH_MAX_PER_ROOM` | int | 4-48 (default 24) **[PLACEHOLDER: `PATCH_MAX_PER_ROOM`]** | tuning | Content bound, not a cull (FT-19) |

Monotone non-decreasing as `T` falls (cold) or rises (soot). `ceil` is used so the count equals the number of selected tiles for an odd `m` (indices 0, 2, ..., m - 1). **Pop bound:** `m` rises by at most `ceil(N x delta_cover_pm / 1000)` per step, and at the cryo-bay heater's 8 mC per step `delta_cover_pm` is 0.53, so for a room of at most 1875 tiles `m` rises by at most 1 and the patch count by at most 1 (never more than `PATCH_STRIDE`) per Graph step, which is the "room is slowly getting cold" read. Placement and variants are deterministic (D.6). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
446	**Example (cryo bay, no leak anchor, `FX-CRYO` geometry stub):** 42 tiles (registry `room_volume` fixture V 42), `T` -2000 mC (FROST, sev 2): `cover_pm` = floor(2000 x 1000 / 15000) = 133, `m` = floor(42 x 133 / 1000) = 5, `n_patches` = `min(24, ceil(5 / 2))` = **3** patches at size s (the anchor patch plus two). It adds no second chain (FT-3: one source, one continuous trail).
469	
470	The `coolant_wet_run` formula is defined as:
471	
472	`frost_px = min(trail_extent_px, frost_reach(T))` ; `n_frost = max(1, n_cover(frost_px))` (D.1; the head fan stamp is always drawn, and stamps `i < n_frost` are frost kind at their D.1 sizes) ; `frost_end_px = start(n_frost)` ; `n_wet = ceil(max(0, trail_extent_px - frost_end_px) / WET_PITCH_PX)` ; wet piece `j` (0 to `n_wet` - 1) at offset `o_j = frost_end_px + WET_PITCH_PX x j` ; `L = (WET_SRC_PX - WET_MIN_PX) / 2 + 1` ; `lvl_j = min(L - 1, floor(o_j x L / edge_len_px))` ; `wet_w_j = WET_SRC_PX - 2 x lvl_j`
473	
474	**Variables:**
475	
476	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
477	|---|---|---|---|---|
478	| `trail_extent_px` | int px | 48 - `edge_len_px` | D.2 (age bound only for this row) | Length of the whole chain, frost plus wet run |
479	| `frost_reach(T)` | int px | 0-1152 | D.3 | The temperature bound, now an appearance bound |
480	| `frost_px` | int px | 0 - `trail_extent_px` | calculated | How much of the chain is drawn as frost |
481	| `n_cover`, `start` | int | - | D.1 | Stamp count and offsets of the frost stamps |
482	| `n_frost` | int | 1 - `n_cover` | calculated | Frost stamps; at least the head fan |
483	| `frost_end_px` | int px | 48 - 1152 | calculated | End of the last frost stamp; wet pieces begin here |
484	| `WET_PITCH_PX` | int px | 48 (fixed, = `STAMP_PX[1]`) | technical-artist | Wet pieces tile at the s pitch whatever the frost stamp sizes |
485	| `WET_SRC_PX` | int px | 6-12, even (default 8) **[PLACEHOLDER: `WET_SRC_PX`]** | tuning | Width of the widest wet piece |
486	| `WET_MIN_PX` | int px | 2 (fixed) | FT-22 minimum feature | Width of the narrowest wet piece |
487	| `L` | int | 3-6 | calculated | Number of width levels |
488	| `edge_len_px` | int px | 48 - `TRAIL_EDGE_MAX_PX` | Layout (D.2) | Polyline length; the width law is keyed to the whole edge, not to the extent, so a piece's width never changes as the trail grows |
489	| `wet_w_j` | int px | `WET_MIN_PX` - `WET_SRC_PX`, even | calculated | Width of piece `j` |
490	
491	**Derivation of the constants.** *Constraint 1 (followable):* a six-tile (288 px) edge must show at least three distinct widths, so a player can order any two points that lie in different thirds of the run: `L` >= 3, hence `WET_SRC_PX` >= `WET_MIN_PX` + 4 = 6. *Constraint 2 (the pixel rules):* a width step is a whole 2 x 2 cell (FT-22), so widths go down in 2 px steps and `WET_MIN_PX` is 2. *Choice:* `WET_SRC_PX` 8 gives `L` 4, one 2 px step per quarter of the edge, the widths 8 / 6 / 4 / 2, and a lateral strip far inside FT-37's 48 px. *Constraint 3 (budget):* frost stamps are at least 48 px long, so `n_frost` <= `frost_end_px` / 48; `frost_end_px` is a multiple of 48 (sums of 48, 96 and 144), so `n_frost + n_wet` <= `frost_end_px` / 48 + ceil((`trail_extent_px` - `frost_end_px`) / 48) = ceil(`trail_extent_px` / 48), which is the 12-cell worst case that D.9 already budgets (a 576 px edge at 48 px stride, plus the accent): the wet run replaces frost slots one for one and `stamps_world` is unchanged.
492	
493	**Output Range:** `wet_w_j` in {2, 4, 6, 8} at the defaults, monotone non-increasing in `o_j`; any two pieces in different width levels differ by at least 2 px in the right order, so any two points more than one level apart (72 px on a 288 px edge) are ordered by width. `n_wet` 0 while the extent is within the head frost stamp (the first `grow_steps` of a fresh fault). The wet run is static and freezes with the extent at the isolation step (FT-8); it dulls by D.5.
494	**Example (COMFORT, the home-ship default):** a sev 3 `1 LEAK/COOLANT` on a 288 px edge, `T` 15000 mC, `grow_steps` 100. D.2: `age_px` = 6 x 100 = 600, `reach_px` = `edge_len_px` 288, extent = `min(288, max(48, min(600, 288)))` = **288**. `frost_reach(15000)` = 0, so `frost_px` 0, `n_frost` = `max(1, n_cover(0))` = 1 (the m head, 96 px), `frost_end_px` = `start(1)` = 96. `n_wet` = ceil((288 - 96) / 48) = **4**, at offsets 96, 144, 192, 240. `L` 4: `lvl` = floor(o x 4 / 288) = 1, 2, 2, 3, so widths **6, 4, 4, 2** px. The chain has 1 + 4 = 5 pieces = `n_cover(288)` (D.1 starts 0, 96, 144, 192, 240, 288), the same count as before the ruling. At `grow_steps` 0 the extent is 48, `n_wet` 0 and only the head fan shows (revealed to 48 of 96 px); the first wet piece appears at `grow_steps` 17 (extent 102, revealed 6 of 48 px, D.10). **Cryo bay warming** (336 px edge, extent 336, `L` 4, level boundaries every 84 px): at wake (`T` -2000, reach 544) `frost_px` 336, `n_frost` 6, `n_wet` 0, all frost. At `T` 6000 (reach 192): `frost_px` 192, `n_frost` = `n_cover(192)` = 3, `frost_end_px` 192, `n_wet` = ceil(144 / 48) = 3 at 192, 240, 288, `lvl` = floor(o x 4 / 336) = 2, 2, 3, widths **4, 4, 2**; 3 + 3 = 6 = `n_cover(336)`. At `T` 10000 (reach 0): `n_frost` 1, `frost_end_px` 96, `n_wet` 5 at 96, 144, 192, 240, 288, `lvl` 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, widths **6, 6, 4, 4, 2**; 1 + 5 = 6. The extent is 336 in all three. A derelict dead coolant fault back-dated past `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` at COMFORT draws the head fan and the whole run, greyed (D.5): the coolant verdict now reads at any temperature.
495	
496	### D.3 `frost_reach`
497	
498	The `frost_reach` formula is defined as:
499	
500	`reach_px = 0` for `T >= T_EDGE[COMFORT/COOL]` ; `reach_px = R_k + floor((T_k - T) x (R_(k+1) - R_k) / (T_k - T_(k+1)))` for `T` between knot `k` (warmer) and knot `k + 1` (colder), when `FROST_REACH_INTERP` is true ; `reach_px = 1152` for `T <= T_EDGE[FREEZING/DEEP_COLD]` ; when `FROST_REACH_INTERP` is false, `reach_px = R_STEP[band(T)]` (a pure per-band step table)
501	
502	The knots `T_k` are the Graph's temperature band edges (LS-7, `LSG:76`-`LSG:102`), **cited by position and never redefined here**: the COMFORT/COOL edge, the COOL/FROST edge, the FROST/FREEZING edge (the Graph's `COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC`) and the FREEZING/DEEP_COLD edge. This GDD supplies only the reach `R_k` at each edge.
503	
504	**Variables:**
505	
506	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
507	|---|---|---|---|---|
508	| `T` | int mC | about -40000 - 70000 | `compartment(cid).T` (true value, polled once per Graph step) | Room temperature; never the perceived value (FT-2) |
509	| `T_k` | int mC | the four LS-7 edges, warm to cold | Graph LS-7 (`LSG:76`-`LSG:102`), cited | Interpolation knots; if LS-7 moves, the knots move with it |
510	| `R_k` | int px | 0 / 480 / 960 / 1152 at the four edges, warm to cold **[PLACEHOLDER: `FROST_REACH_PX`]**, monotone, range 0-1152 | tuning | Reach at each band edge |
511	| `R_STEP[band]` | int px | COMFORT and warmer 0; COOL 480; FROST 960; FREEZING 1152; DEEP_COLD 1152 **[PLACEHOLDER: `FROST_REACH_PX`]** | tuning | Used only when `FROST_REACH_INTERP` is false (value at the band's colder edge) |
512	| `FROST_REACH_INTERP` | bool | default true **[PLACEHOLDER: `FROST_REACH_INTERP`]** | tuning (CP-7) | False restores the literal per-band table; retreat then jumps up to 480 px at a band key |
513	| `reach_px` | int px | 0-1152 | calculated | Maximum frost spread: the temperature bound of D.2 for `4 FREEZE`, and the bound of `frost_px` for `1 LEAK/COOLANT` (D.2d) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
514	
515	**Output Range:** 0..1152, non-increasing in `T` (monotone; a test sweeps `T` and asserts it). The largest intermediate product is 15000 x 480 = 7,200,000 (the widest segment, COOL/FROST to FROST/FREEZING), which fits int32. **Fixture floor (FT-11, knob constraint):** `frost_reach(T = -2000 mC)` >= 336 px (a function of `T` alone; the age bound is separate, D.2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
516	**Example:** `T` -2000 mC lies between the COOL/FROST edge (`T_k` 0, `R_k` 480) and the FROST/FREEZING edge (-15000, 960): `480 + floor(2000 x 480 / 15000)` = 480 + 64 = **544** (>= 336, so the fixture floor holds). `T` 6000 mC, between the COMFORT/COOL edge (10000, 0) and the COOL/FROST edge (0, 480): `floor(4000 x 480 / 10000)` = **192**. `T` -20000 mC, between the FROST/FREEZING edge (-15000, 960) and the FREEZING/DEEP_COLD edge (-40000, 1152): `960 + floor(5000 x 192 / 25000)` = 960 + 38 = **998**. With `FROST_REACH_INTERP` false the same three temperatures give 960, 480 and 1152. (The edge values quoted are LS-7's as of this writing and are the Graph's to move.)
517	
518	### D.4 `trail_density`
519	
520	The `trail_density` formula is defined as:
521	
522	`bucket = floor(intensity_pm / 100)` (0..10) ; `density_level = 0 if intensity_pm = 0 else 1 + min(3, floor(bucket / DENSITY_BUCKETS_PER_LEVEL))` ; for the ten ids with no Graph `intensity_pm` (FT-30), `density_level = sev` (static cover only; `27 PATCH_WEEP` is sev 1 only) and the moving media run iff the row's LIVE predicate holds: `2 SHORT` iff the faulted conductor's `flow` > 0 (arc pops), `3 OVERHEAT` iff the machine's `T` is above the Graph's OVERHEAT_OFF edge (`OVERHEAT_OFF_MC`, cited, Graph-owned; shimmer), and no other of the ten has a moving medium (`7 OVERLOAD`, `9 SCRAM`, `4 FREEZE`, `27 PATCH_WEEP` and `20 ATMO_COLD` / `21 ATMO_HOT` draw static stamps only; `22` and `23` draw nothing) ; `cover16 = 0 if density_level = 0 else max(DITHER_MIN_CELLS, COVER16_FLOOR[row], 4 x density_level)` with `COVER16_FLOOR[row]` = 8 for the **seam-weep mist** (`1 LEAK/GAS` on a SEAM subject) and 0 for every other row *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: at `A_seam` 1 the weep is about 15 permille, level 1, 4 of 16 cells on a 16 px puff lit only by the lamp, which can read as "nothing is wrong")* ; the sev 3+ anchor accent (FT-5) is drawn at `cover16 = 16` whatever the flow ; `drip_per_s = DRIP_PER_S[density_level]` ; `frames_active = FRAMES_ACTIVE[density_level]`
523	
524	This system never states a formula for the Graph's `intensity_pm` (leak rate, hole area, AIRFLOW `|dP|`: `LSG:158`); it only buckets the value the descriptor carries, on the Graph's own 100-permille quantum so a level change always coincides with an `F/` key (`LSG:201`, D.10 `dirty_key_budget`).
525	
526	**Variables:**
527	
528	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
529	|---|---|---|---|---|
530	| `intensity_pm` | int | 0-1000 | descriptor (`LSG:158`) | Flow fraction in permille; 0 = STILL (FT-17) |
531	| `DENSITY_BUCKETS_PER_LEVEL` | int | **2-3** (default 3) **[PLACEHOLDER: `DENSITY_BUCKETS_PER_LEVEL`]** | tuning | Level width in 100-permille buckets. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the range was 2-5, but `bucket` tops out at 10 and level 4 needs `bucket` >= 3 x the width, so a width of 4 or 5 made level 4 unreachable inside the legal range; the range is now 2-3 and AC-167 sweeps it.)* |
532	| `density_level` | int | 0-4 | calculated | 0 = STILL (no moving media), 1-4 otherwise |
533	| `DITHER_MIN_CELLS` | int | 2 (fixed floor) | technical-artist | A non-zero density never draws fewer than 2 of the 16 cells of the 4 x 4 ordered dither (a lone 2 x 2 cell per 8 x 8 reads as noise, so 1 of 16 is never used); it is the absolute guard under every `COVER16_FLOOR` (a floor below 2 but above 0 is a lint error) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
534	| `COVER16_FLOOR[row]` | int | 0 or 2-16 (default 8 for the seam-weep mist, 0 otherwise) **[PLACEHOLDER: `COVER16_FLOOR`]** | tuning (design review) | Per-row legibility floor on `cover16`; the seam mist is the first row that exceeds the dither minimum *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
535	| `cover16` | int | 0, 4, 8, 12, 16 | calculated | Lit cells of a world-anchored 4 x 4 ordered dither of 2 x 2-px cells (binary alpha, never partial alpha: FT-23) |
536	| `DRIP_PER_S[level]` | int/s | {0, 1, 2, 4, 6} **[PLACEHOLDER: `DRIP_PER_S`]** | tuning | Drops per second; 6/s is one drop per 2 frames at 12 fps |
537	| `FRAMES_ACTIVE[level]` | int | {0, 2, 4, 6, 6} **[PLACEHOLDER: `FRAMES_ACTIVE`]** | tuning | Active frames of vent, dust and debris strips |
538	
539	**Output Range:** `density_level` is 0 only when STILL; otherwise 1..4. Boundaries at the default width 3: `intensity_pm` 1-299 -> 1; 300-599 -> 2; 600-899 -> 3; 900-1000 -> 4; at the minimum width 2: 1-199 -> 1; 200-399 -> 2; 400-599 -> 3; 600-1000 -> 4 (level 4 is reachable at both legal widths). (orchestrator ruling: the technical-artist proposed a ten-tier `ceil(intensity_pm / 100)` ladder; the written FT-30 and transition T7 already assume a `density_level` scheme, so the four-level scheme is kept and the technical-artist's finding survives as the `DITHER_MIN_CELLS` floor.) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
540	**Example:** a hull breach whose descriptor carries `intensity_pm` 625 (taken as given from the Graph's hole-area scaling): `bucket` 6, `density_level` = 1 + min(3, floor(6 / 3)) = 3, `cover16` 12 of 16, and the debris and wind strips run `FRAMES_ACTIVE[3]` = 6 frames. A trickle at `intensity_pm` 80: `bucket` 0, level 1, `cover16` 4, 1 drop per second, 2 active frames. The seam weep at `A_seam` 1 (`intensity_pm` 15): level 1, `cover16` = max(2, 8, 4) = **8**, 2 active frames. The same plate at its pre-stage (`intensity_pm` 0): level 0, hairline only. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
541	
542	### D.5 `dullness`
543	
544	The `dullness` formula is defined as:
545	
546	`dull_pm = min(1000, floor(mode_steps x 1000 / DRIED_AFTER_STEPS))` ; `dull_step = DULL_STEPS - 1 if mode_steps >= DRIED_AFTER_STEPS else floor(mode_steps x (DULL_STEPS - 1) / DRIED_AFTER_STEPS)` ; `glow_step = max(0, GLOW_STEPS - floor(dull_pm x GLOW_STEPS / EMISSIVE_OFF_DULL_PM))` ; `dull_step_shown = min(dull_step, DULL_STEPS - 2)` while `cap_applies` and `dull_step` otherwise, with `cap_applies` = the descriptor is LIVE (D.4: `intensity_pm` > 0, or the row's LIVE predicate true) or its row is an ongoing static row (7 OVERLOAD, 27 PATCH_WEEP; FT-17; 4 FREEZE and 9 SCRAM are latched faults and are not capped) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* ; fuel only: `fuel_dried = (dull_step_shown = DULL_STEPS - 1)`, a palette swap with no intermediate stop and no dither *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: (1) the age is `mode_steps`, the trail's own mode age, GA-T, so a pipe that wore for 30 minutes and then leaks starts at `dull_step` 0 and `fuel_dried` false; (2) the final, dried stop is reached only at `mode_steps` >= `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` (the ramp's end, `dull_pm` 1000), so it can never start before the 7500-step floor, and the steps below it divide the ramp evenly; (3) `fuel_dried` flips at the final stop only, not at half the ramp; (4) the integer forms are explicit, so an odd `DULL_STEPS` is defined)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: `dull_step_shown`, the LIVE cap, Open Questions 6d.)*
547	
548	Dullness is the visual consequence of age, with **one LIVE cap** (default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), Open Questions 6d): below the dried stop there is no LIVE term in the ramp (CP-8), so a live leak and an isolated one of the same `mode_steps` carry the same `dull_step`, but a LIVE descriptor is shown at most at stop `DULL_STEPS` - 2, so no live trail ever wears the dried verdict. `mode_steps` restarts at every mode entry and every `sev` change, so a live trail is young by construction; the one exception, a leak isolated early and reopened after `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` steps (live with a dried-stop age), is what the cap catches: it is shown at stop `DULL_STEPS` - 2, aged but not dried. The cap releases on the frame the descriptor stops being LIVE, so an isolation lands the dried stop in one palette step (intended: the leak is old and the valve is the player's own act; AC-36 therefore holds for every `mode_steps` below `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`, and AC-177 covers the exception). **The cap's reach** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a row with no LIVE axis whose descriptor is an ongoing condition (7 OVERLOAD, 27 PATCH_WEEP) is held at the same stop for as long as the descriptor exists (state DRAWN_STATIC, no release), and a latched fault (4 FREEZE, 9 SCRAM) is not capped (FT-17, AC-177). `glow_step` stays on the uncapped `dull_pm`: the emissive rows with a LIVE predicate (rows 2 and 3) are moving media (arc pops, shimmer) that are never dulled, and the always-static emissive rows (7, 9) have no LIVE state to cap. It applies to **static stamps only**; moving media (drip, mist, debris, arc pops) are never dulled (FT-17). The emissive overlay of a static scorch, arc box or ember edge follows `glow_step`, one function of `dull_pm` (so SCRAM's decaying rim and every other overlay share one rule); the arc *pops* (a moving medium) are never dulled and continue while the descriptor lives. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
549	
550	**Variables:**
551	
552	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
553	|---|---|---|---|---|
554	| `mode_steps` | int | 0 - unbounded | descriptor, **GA-T (adopted, LS-14)**: `step_no - mode_since_step`, unfrozen by isolation, dominant descriptor only (a non-dominant NODE or EDGE descriptor takes `dull_step` 0, FT-8) | Age of the current mode and severity; derelict dead faults are authored large by back-dating `mode_since_step` (`LSG:226`, Derelict Authoring D.11) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
555	| `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` | int | 7500-36000 (default 12000 = 20 min) **[PLACEHOLDER: `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`]** | tuning (CP-8) | `mode_steps` at which the ramp ends and the dried stop is reached. Lower bound 7500 = 12.5 min, the longest live MVP clock (`LSG:667` D.15), so no live fault reaches the dried look before it finishes; upper bound 36000 (1 h) so authored derelict faults can reach it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
556	| `dull_pm` | int | 0-1000 | calculated | Permille of the ramp |
557	| `DULL_STEPS` | int | 4-8, any integer (default 4) **[PLACEHOLDER: `DULL_STEPS`]** | tuning (CP-8) | Number of palette steps, the last of which is the dried stop (the art-director's scan-matrix alternative is 8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
558	| `dull_step` | int | 0..`DULL_STEPS` - 1 | calculated | Index into the per-medium stop table; at 4 steps the fresh-hue cells of the 16-cell dither are `HUE_CELLS` = {16, 11, 5, 0} (Ice, Amber, Cyan only; the table is authored per `DULL_STEPS` in the asset spec) |
559	| `dull_step_shown` | int | 0..`DULL_STEPS` - 1 | calculated | The stop the palette actually draws: `dull_step`, capped at `DULL_STEPS` - 2 while `cap_applies` (the descriptor is LIVE, or its row is an ongoing static row 7 or 27). Constraint: the live stop must sit strictly below the dried stop, `DULL_STEPS` - 2 < `DULL_STEPS` - 1, and be at least 0, which holds for every legal `DULL_STEPS` (4-8 gives a cap of 2-6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
560	| `GLOW_STEPS` | int | 4 (fixed) | technical-artist | Quantisation of the emissive overlay level |
561	| `EMISSIVE_OFF_DULL_PM` | int | 250-750 (default 500) **[PLACEHOLDER: `EMISSIVE_OFF_DULL_PM`]** | tuning (CP-8) | `dull_pm` at which the overlay is fully off; expressed in permille so it is independent of `DULL_STEPS` |
562	| `glow_step` | int | 0..`GLOW_STEPS` | calculated | 4 = peak overlay, 0 = off |
563	| `fuel_dried` | bool | - | calculated | Fuel Ember draws for every step below the last, the dried stop at the last step only; never a mix (any blend of Fuel Ember with a grey passes through the flesh band: technical-artist consult) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
564	
565	**Output Range:** `dull_step` 0..`DULL_STEPS` - 1, monotone non-decreasing in `mode_steps`, 0 at `mode_steps` 0, equal to `DULL_STEPS` - 1 only at `mode_steps` >= `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`; `glow_step` monotone non-increasing, 0 for `dull_pm` >= `EMISSIVE_OFF_DULL_PM`. Every dried stop is a palette hex and the floor of every ramp is Hull Grey (contrast 1.90:1 against Graphite lit, `TRAIL_MIN_CONTRAST_X100` 190); Hull Grey is a thin-element colour, so dried interiors are drawn as edges and stains, never as a plane. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
566	**Example (defaults 12000 and 4: the stops change at `mode_steps` 4000, 8000 and 12000, 6.7 minutes apart):** the cryo-bay leak at `mode_steps` 168: `dull_pm` = floor(168000 / 12000) = 14, `dull_step` 0, `glow_step` 4 (no overlay on coolant anyway). The same leak at 4000 (6.7 min): `dull_pm` 333, `dull_step` = floor(4000 x 3 / 12000) = 1 (11 of 16 cells Ice, 5 Hull Grey), still dripping: slightly aged; at 3999 it is still 0. A SCRAM scorch at 3000: `dull_pm` 250, `glow_step` = max(0, 4 - floor(250 x 4 / 500)) = 2, a half-strength rim. A derelict dead frost fan back-dated to 18000: `dull_pm` 1000 (clamped), `dull_step` 3 (all Hull Grey). A derelict fuel stain at 40000: `dull_step` 3 = `DULL_STEPS` - 1, so `fuel_dried` (the dried stop, an ember-dim stain with value descending first: the art-director's rule, Visual/Audio). **A live fuel leak at `mode_steps` 7500 (the longest live MVP clock): `dull_step` 1, `fuel_dried` false** (the former half-ramp rule gave `fuel_dried` true from 6000). **Wear then leak:** a fuel pipe that was WORN for 30 minutes and then crosses `LEAK_HP` has `mode_steps` 0 at its first LEAK frame: `dull_step` 0, `fuel_dried` false, even though its `since_steps` is 18000. **Odd width:** `DULL_STEPS` 5 gives stops at 3000, 6000, 9000 and 12000. **Live cap (default applied 2026-10-27):** at the defaults a coolant leak isolated at `mode_steps` 3000, left, and reopened at `mode_steps` 15000 is live; `dull_step` there is 3 (all Hull Grey, the dried stop), and `dull_step_shown` = min(3, 4 - 2) = **2** (5 of 16 Ice cells: aged, not dried); the same history on a fuel leak keeps `fuel_dried` false; the valve closes one step later, the descriptor is STILL, the cap releases and the stop is 3 (and `fuel_dried` true) in that one frame. A derelict dead fault (`intensity_pm` 0, never LIVE) is unaffected. **Ongoing static rows (re-review):** a `7 OVERLOAD` scorch or a `27 PATCH_WEEP` weep present at `mode_steps` 15000 shows `dull_step_shown` 2, not 3; a derelict `4 FREEZE` sheath or `9 SCRAM` scorch at 15000 shows 3 (the dried verdict), uncapped. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings; re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
