The `zoom_ladder` formula (registry: `zoom_out_k`) is defined as:

`k_z ∈ {1, 2, …, k_base + 2}`, `k_z ← clamp(k_z ± 1, 1, k_base + 2)` on each `zoom_out` / `zoom_in` edge press — **the lower bound `1` is the default `ZOOM_MIN_K`; the effective ladder is `[ZOOM_MIN_K(k_base, target), k_base + 2]`, a static data table that withholds the bottom steps that fail D.16's cap (predicted-withheld table in D.16; at the large targets this is the expected outcome, not an edge case), and every "ladder" in this GDD is read as the effective ladder** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (persistent; `k_z ← k_base` on re-wake and at boot); field under `expand` `(2·floor(W / (2·k_z)), 2·floor(H / (2·k_z)))` (uncapped); field under `keep` `(2·floor(320·k_base / k_z), 2·floor(180·k_base / k_z))` — **always an even integer pair, the remainder letterboxed** (a 426.67×240 field on the Deck at `k_z` 3 and a 548.57×308.57 field at 2160p, `k_z` 7, are not renderable; they are 426×240 and 548×308), so the world picture is `field · k_z`, centred inside the HUD rect, which stays pinned to the `k_base` picture (remainder < 2·`k_z` px per axis) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `tiles = field / 48`; sprite ratio `k_z / k_base`; field-scale factor `s = field_h / 360`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| k_auto | int | 2 – unbounded | D.1 | Automatic world scale for the window |
| k_base | int | 2 – k_auto | D.1 / Settings | **Effective base scale**: the manual `k` when Settings sets one below Auto (PR-2, PR-14; aspect is then `keep`), else `k_auto`. It is the default zoom step, the anchor of the ladder `[1, k_base + 2]` and the `k` of the HUD rect's picture, everywhere this GDD writes it; **`H_default` stays `max(k_auto, 3)`** — the HUD follows the display, not the player's manual world scale, so the registry `hud_multiplier` is unchanged *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| k_z | int | 1 – k_base + 2 | calculated (player's edge presses) | Current ladder step; `k_z = k_base` is default; never held, never saved |
| field | int pair (even) | 320×180 (k_base + 2 on a 1280×720 picture; 384×216 at 1080p) – 1920×1080 (1× at 1080p); 1440 rows at 1× on 1440p; 3840×2160 at 1× on 2160p *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)* | calculated | Logical size of the world viewport at the step |
| tiles | float pair | 8 × 4.5 – 40 × 22.5 at 1080p | calculated | Visible field in 48-px tiles |
| k_z / k_base | float | 1/k_base – (k_base + 2)/k_base (0.33 – 1.67 at 1080p) | calculated | Apparent sprite scale; integer scaling never resamples, so marks are intact at every step — the *perceived* size below 50 % is the acuity question routed to the accessibility-specialist |
| s | float | 0.5 – 6.0 (180 – 2160 rows: 0.5 at `k_z` 4 on a 1280×720 `keep` picture, 6.0 at `k_z` 1 on 2160p; the 0.6 – 4.0 printed before excluded both ends) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion)* | calculated | Scales the solver's length parameters (`L_MAX`, `L_SLEW_MAX`, `LAG_CUT`, `JUMP_CUT`; D.7, D.10) and the inner box (D.8) by `s`, and `τ_follow` (D.6) by `min(1, s)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

**Output Range:** Bounded on both ends by the ladder; a press beyond either end is ignored (`diag.zoom_step_refused`). The field is uncapped on purpose (Section C PR-6 C6): PR-2's 960×540 cap applies to the default step only. Each step is a one-frame cut; no intermediate scale exists; `Camera2D.zoom` stays `(1,1)`. `k_base + 2` at 1080p (5×) shows 8 × 4.5 tiles — less than a beam's reach — accepted as the player's own choice. 1× at 1080p is 9× the default field (lit pixels under pass A, Y-sorted content); 1× on the Deck is 4×.
**Example:** 1080p (`k_base = 3`): ladder 1 / 2 / **3** / 4 / 5 → fields 1920×1080 / 960×540 / 640×360 / 480×270 / 384×216 (40 × 22.5 … 8 × 4.5 tiles), sprite ratios 0.33 / 0.67 / 1 / 1.33 / 1.67, `s` = 3.0 / 1.5 / 1 / 0.75 / 0.6, and the `τ_follow` factor `min(1, s)` = 1 / 1 / 1 / 0.75 / 0.6 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. 1440p (`k_base = 4`): ladder 1–6; one step out (`k_z` = 3) is 852×480 = 17.75 × 10 tiles, two steps out (`k_z` = 2) is 1280×720 = 26.7 × 15 tiles *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Deck under `expand` (`k_base = 2`): ladder 1 / **2** / 3 / 4 → 1280×800 / 640×400 / 426×266 / 320×200 (all even); `keep` on the Deck, 1280×720 picture: 1 / **2** / 3 / 4 → 1280×720 / 640×360 / 426×240 (2 px residual per axis, 1 black column each side) / 320×180; 1× is 26.7 × 16.7 tiles — under pass A its render target is 4× the lit pixels of the default field (pass B: unchanged); see E for the draw-call and lighting consequence.

**D.6 Follow (first-order exponential approach)**

The `follow` formula (registry: `camera_follow`) is defined as:

`dt' = min(dt, DT_MAX)` with `DT_MAX` = 0.05 s, and the update is **skipped when `dt ≤ 0`**; `τ_follow_eff = τ_follow × min(1, s)`, `s = field_h / 360` (D.5; `s = 1` at the default step); **if `τ_follow_eff ≤ τ_EPS` (1e-4 s) then `a = 1`** (rigid follow, no `0/0`), else `a = 1 − exp(−dt' / τ_follow_eff)`; `f_n = f_{n−1} + a · (target_n − f_{n−1})` per axis; **settle: if `|target_n − f_n| < SETTLE_EPS` (= 0.5·Q) then `f_n = target_n`**; lag is measured **after** the update, `lag_n = |target_n − f_n|`, and for a constant-velocity target `lag_ss(dt) = v · τ_follow_eff · h / (e^h − 1)` with `h = dt/τ_follow_eff` — strictly below, and approaching as `dt → 0`, the limit `lag_∞ = v · τ_follow_eff` that Section G uses as the conservative bound; settle times `t_95 = 3 · τ_follow_eff` and `t_settle_f = τ_follow_eff · ln(|d₀| / SETTLE_EPS)` (the whole-pose settle is `max(t_settle_f, t_settle_L)`, `t_settle_L` from D.7, ≈ 2.5 s after a full aim reversal; `SETTLE_EPS` is per axis, on `f` and `L` separately) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; solver state is float64 scalars per axis *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check: field scaling added; Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `min(1, s)`, guards, settle, lag measured after the update, float64)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| dt | float | 0.004 – 0.05 s (clamped to `DT_MAX` = 0.05; a hitch longer than that advances the solver by 0.05 s and the remainder is a target discontinuity for D.10) | engine (render delta) | Frame time *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| τ_follow (registry: `FOLLOW_TAU`) | float | 0.18 s (safe 0 – < 0.20 at the 360-row field: 0.20 gives `108 > 108`, which fails the strict inner-box invariant; > 0.267 breaks the lag-cut invariant) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, registry alignment; Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: strict bound)* | tuning (G) | Follow time constant; 0 = rigid follow (the step-12 A/B) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| target_n | float pair | body px | kernel read view, interpolated (D.9) | Avatar's interpolated position this frame |
| f_n | float pair | body px | calculated | The follow component of the camera pose, before look-ahead, clamp and quantisation |
| v | float | 0 – v_max (base px/s) | Player Controller GDD (`v_walk` 120, `v_run` = `v_max` 180; registry `V_WALK` / `V_RUN`) | Avatar speed |
| s | float | 0.5 – 6.0 (180 – 2160 rows, D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, registry alignment)* | D.5 | Field-scale factor; `τ` scales by `min(1, s)` so the frame never keeps drifting longer than at the default step (the old `τ·s` meant a 1.6 s settle after stopping at `s = 3`, against Game Feel "Stillness"); lag as a fraction of the frame is constant for `s ≤ 1` and smaller for `s > 1`; the on-screen lag in screen px is constant for `s ≤ 1` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| lag_ss | float | 0 – v_max·τ_follow_eff | calculated | Distance the camera trails a constant-velocity avatar, measured after the update (D.6 formula; `lag_∞ = v·τ_follow_eff` is its dt→0 limit and upper bound) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| SETTLE_EPS | float | 0.5·Q base px (0.5 at `Q = 1`) | tuning (G) | Per-axis snap distance for `f` and `L` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| t_95 | float | 0 – 0.9 s | calculated | Time to close 95 % of a step |

**Output Range:** `a ∈ (0, 1]` for any positive `dt'` (1 only for rigid follow), so `f` moves monotonically toward the target with zero overshoot — the camera never reverses unless the target does (C-R) — and equals the target exactly once the settle fires. For a target held constant through the frame, two 144-fps frames and one 60-fps frame of equal total `dt` give the same `f` to floating-point precision (per-frame factor 0.0884 at 60 fps, 0.0378 at 144 fps); for a **moving** target the per-frame update is not exact and the lag it holds depends on `dt`. **Where lag is measured: after the update, against `target_n`** (the pose the clamp and `P_lag` see, and the frame that is drawn). At `v_max` = 180 and `τ = 0.18`: 32.0 px at 240 fps, 31.8 at 144, 31.4 at 90, 30.9 at 60, 30.2 at 40, 29.5 at 30, 28.1 at `DT_MAX` — always below `lag_∞` = 32.4 (at `v_walk` = 120: 21.4 / 21.2 / 20.9 / 20.6 / 20.1 / 19.7 / 18.7 against 21.6). The 0.9 px spread between 60 and 144 fps is the whole frame-rate dependence on a continuous trace, which is why the contract is "within 1 base px" (C3). The **inner-box margin therefore does not erode at low fps down to about 15 fps** (the finding that it does measured the lag before the update; after it, the lag only shrinks) — **below 15 fps it does**: the catch-up cap moves the target up to 12 px per frame and the after-update lag reaches 37.4 px, so `37.4 + 72 = 109.4 > 108` and the box engages by 1.4 px (Section G) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — 
**Example:** A synthetic 40 px single-frame target step (no legal movement produces one; D.10) at 60 fps, default field: frame 1 `f` moves 3.54 px, after 6 frames (0.1 s) 17.05 px, and the 38.0 px level (95 %) is first reached on **frame 33** (38.12 px; frame 32 is 37.93 px); a 100 px step is within 5 px from frame 33 (4.71 px). Running at `v_max` = 180 px/s the camera trails by `lag_∞` = 32.4 px (30.9 px measured after the update at 60 fps); at walk (120 px/s) 21.6 px (20.6 at 60 fps) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. At the 270-row zoom-in field (`s = 0.75`, `τ_follow_eff = 0.135 s`) the same run trails by 24.3 px and the walk by 16.2 px — 9 % and 6 % of the field in both cases; at the 540-row zoom-out field (`s = 1.5`) `τ_follow_eff` stays 0.18 s (`min(1, s)`), the run trails by 32.4 px (6 % of the field) and the frame settles in the same 0.54 s as at the default step *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.

content.thinking:
Checking the deck's smaller region sizes, both 320×180 and 320×200 configurations fall well under the 9,216 px minimum, which contradicts the claim that this threshold represents the smallest region any display can present—so the D.8b flash clamp may not actually hold on RM-DECK.

Looking closer, the Pipeline GDD itself explicitly lists 320×180 as a valid field size at k_base+2 on a 1280×720 picture, meaning the 720p Deck mode is a legitimately supported configuration, not an edge case. This means REGION_MIN_PX, if derived only from 1080p assumptions, understates the true minimum region size and the photosensitivity safety math built on it is non-conservative—worth flagging as a safety concern, though I need to figure out whether it rises to blocking severity given that R12 made Deck an explicit reference target.

I run the numbers properly: the 320×180 displayed picture divided into a 3×3 grid gives a region floor of 106×60 = 6,360 px. Computing the swing for a one-letter arc at that region size yields about 13%, which exceeds the 10% threshold for counting as a flash—so at the Deck's zoomed-in max step, a flickering arc would register as a counted flash event, though since the flash rate itself still stays within the 3/s limit, this seems more like an erosion of safety margin than an outright violation of the hard flash-rate cap.

This means the invariant that the clamp holds "at every field and every pan" is actually false for the 320×180 field size. I'd recommend re-deriving REGION_MIN_PX from the Pipeline's smallest field and propagating that through the swing calculations. I also notice the D.9 display table omits the RM-DECK 1280×800 reference machine entirely, which should be flagged since its field sizes fall within existing ranges but the device itself is a reference target that deserves explicit listing. Checking further, I confirm 720p support generates a 320×180 field as expected from the Pipeline variables, and I catch that D.8b incorrectly claims 384×216 as the smallest field at 1080p when the Pipeline's own numbers show 320×180 is smaller—a factual error worth logging with appropriate severity.

I'm leaning toward RECOMMENDED severity rather than BLOCKING, since the hard 3/s photosensitivity limit still holds through the linter even though the stated invariant is technically violated—unless the acceptance criteria only test at 384×216, in which case the implementation could genuinely be wrong at the smaller field size. I want to check AC-62 through AC-66 and the broader acceptance criteria section against the formulas, then skim the Edge Cases and Tuning Knobs sections to see if this gap is already addressed there.

750	*Rule ids are this GDD's `FT-n`; formulas are `D.n` in Formulas. Every outcome is a pure consequence of the descriptor, Layout geometry and the camera (FT-1): where an edge case seems to need memory, the outcome below says what the stateless reading is. "The Graph" owns every state change named here; this system only redraws.*
751	
752	### Zero, maximum and out-of-range values
753	
754	- **If a descriptor carries `sev` 0** (the Graph emits no mode 1-26 descriptor for a subject at `hp` >= `HP_OK`): nothing is drawn. `sev` 0 is the no-trail state (FT-6). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the PROVISIONAL sev-0 seam exception is retired; the Graph states the seam weep at sev 1, `LSG:170`, so no sev-0 descriptor remains to draw.)*
755	- **If a subject carries the WORN descriptor** (`medium` NONE; the Graph's D.4 gives a subject at `hp` just below `HP_OK` sev 1): nothing is drawn, because WORN is the module-body channel and has no consequence-channel medium, not because its `sev` is 0 (FT-32). The sprite wear, gauge and inspect card are the module presenter's. A *patched* subject at its `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000 cap does not carry WORN: it carries `27 PATCH_WEEP` ("a patch is never silent", `LSG:381`), which draws by row 27 (FT-32). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
756	- **If a descriptor has `medium` != NONE and `sev` >= 1 but no row of the table of record matches its id** (the Graph's ids are append-only forever, so a later Graph version can add one): the unknown id draws nothing and writes one diagnostic line per session; the build-time lint "every descriptor id has a row" (`LSG:1110`'s consumer scan) fails first. A silent fallback to a generic mark is rejected because a generic mark is a trail with no vocabulary (FT-3, `ART:669`).
757	- **If `grow_steps` is 0** (the mode or the severity began this step: a LEAK that has just crossed `LEAK_HP`, a sev change, a seam welded this step): the source stamp draws at `MIN_EXTENT_PX` 48 (D.2), already thickest at the source, and moving media start on the next `present_time` frame. Never an empty first frame: a live descriptor draws on its first step (FT-8). `dull_step` is 0 and `fuel_dried` false on that frame, whatever `since_steps` says (a pipe that wore for 30 minutes and then leaks is born fresh). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
758	- **If `grow_steps` exceeds `SINCE_CLAMP` 20000**: the age bound stops growing at `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[sev] x 20000` (always above any legal `edge_len_px`), so extent equals the edge; `dull_pm` clamps at 1000 (D.5); no overflow is possible because the product is at most 18 x 65535. At the default `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` 12000, a derelict dead fault back-dated to 40000 steps therefore reads exactly like one back-dated to 20000: the verdict does not age further (the clamp bounds the age term of D.2 only; D.5 reads `mode_steps` unclamped, so dullness is unaffected by `SINCE_CLAMP` at any `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: field names.)*
759	- **If `edge_len_px` is below 48** (a one-tile stub): the source stamp is clipped to the edge by the reveal threshold (D.10), never scaled; no pixel leaves the edge (FT-37).
760	- **If `edge_len_px` exceeds `TRAIL_EDGE_MAX_PX` 1152**: it is a Layout content error (lint to Layout and Derelict Authoring); the trail still draws to the length Layout gave, never hidden and never silently shortened, because shortening would hide a consequence-channel element (FT-19).
761	- **If the room's `T` is below the DEEP_COLD edge or above the SCORCH edge** (outside the knots of D.3): `frost_reach` clamps at 1152 or 0 (D.3); frost never extends beyond the edge, and a SCORCH room shows no frost reach at all (only the local stamp); a coolant leak's wet run still runs to the age-bound extent at any temperature (D.2d) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
762	- **If `intensity_pm` is 299 on one step and 300 on the next** (a density-level boundary at the default width): the level steps 1 -> 2 on the same step as the Graph's `F/` key for that 100-permille bucket (D.4), so cover, drip cadence and frame count change once, on the key, and never between keys.
763	- **If a coolant leak is isolated the instant it starts** (`intensity_pm` 0, `isolated_at_step` = `mode_since_step`, so `grow_steps` 0 for ever): the descriptor is STILL at once; the system draws the source stamp (extent `MIN_EXTENT_PX`, frozen) and the sev 3+ anchor accent in full colour, no drip, no moving media (FT-17). Static stamps carry no remembered density: they draw at the authored coverage for the current `sev`, because "held" density would be state (FT-1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
764	- **If an edge's `sev` is 3 and its `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[3]` of 6 px/step runs in the cryo bay**: the front moves at 60 px/s, below the drip's 72 px/s (D.2 invariant iv), so "nothing in the cryo bay moves faster than the drip" (`ART:142`) holds. Raising `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[3]` above 7 breaks it and is refused by the knob range.
765	
766	### Simultaneous rules and handovers
767	
768	- **If two descriptors of different `mode` share one anchor** (a `2 SHORT` and a `3 OVERHEAT` at one junction box): two trails draw, in ascending (`subject_id`, `mode`) order, each with its own extent, size and rows (FT-3). Their emissive overlays overlap additively and count once per pixel toward `TRAIL_OVERDRAW_MAX` 4 (D.9).
769	- **If a severity change and a band change arrive in one Graph step** (a plate drops to sev 4 while the room crosses a band): the `N/` and `B/` keys are delivered together; the next render callback applies both, so there is no frame with the new size and the old frost reach, and no intermediate state exists to draw (FT-15).
770	- **If a coolant pipe's FREEZE descriptor clears and a `1 LEAK/COOLANT` descriptor appears on the same step** (thaw-burst): the frost sheath despawns on the next frame and a new fan spawns at `grow_steps` 0 (extent 48, then growing at the new `sev`'s rate); the room's `20 ATMO_COLD` crust is a separate descriptor and stays while its band stays (row 4, row 20). The handover is two Graph facts, not an animation.
771	- **If a valve closes on a live coolant or fuel leak**: `intensity_pm` falls to 0 and the descriptor stays: DRAWN_LIVE -> DRAWN_STILL (T3). The drip stops and the fan, collar or streak **stays, still, not gone**; **its extent stops growing at the isolation step** (`grow_steps` is frozen, GA-T: a valve closing at `grow_steps` 50 on a sev 3 coolant leak leaves the extent at 300 px 100 steps later); it dulls with `mode_steps` (D.5), and frost recedes only as the room's temperature rises (FT-11). An old isolated leak looks old, which is honest (FT-17). **If the valve is reopened**, `grow_steps` rejoins `mode_steps` and the extent steps once to the age bound of the full mode age, capped by the edge (and, for a `4 FREEZE`, the temperature bound): the leak resumes at its true age; the one-time step is intended and flagged for the Graph owner, who may instead shift the onset by the isolated interval (the resolver renders whatever `grow_steps` is). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
772	- **If a patch lands on a frosted coolant pipe** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the fan, the wet run and the drip vanish the next frame and, on that same frame, the pipe's `27 PATCH_WEEP/COOLANT` appears as one small static s-frost spur at the fitting (a same-step handover: the LEAK descriptor ends, T5, and the weep begins at `mode_steps` 0, T11); the room's `ATMO_COLD` crust (row 20, sev >= 2) stays while the band is FROST or colder. The vanish is a Graph change the player caused, so the art-director's "no stamp disappears in one frame without a player-caused Graph change" holds. The onboarding sentence "patch it" (`LSG:839`) therefore replaces the long carried frost with a small weep, not an empty floor; reconciling it with the valve-based anchor moment is Onboarding's. For a patched duct (`27 PATCH_WEEP/GAS`) the plume ends and nothing new is drawn: the HISS is the tell (FT-18). When the patch later decays and the pipe re-leaks, the weep ends and the new LEAK descriptor begins at `grow_steps` 0 on the same step.
773	- **If a SEAM descriptor is the weep of an imperfect weld** (`1 LEAK/GAS`, sev 1, `intensity_pm` per LS-14 field provenance, counted from `built_step`, `LSG:170`): it draws at s-*trace* along the bead (FT-14) with the mist legibility floor `COVER16_FLOOR` 8, so a physically leaking seam is never undrawn and the first weld the player inspects reads as mist along a seam (P1). When wear-in takes `leak_bp` to 0 the descriptor ends and the trace vanishes the next frame (a Graph change). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the sev-0 exception that stood here is retired.)*
774	- **If a SEAL_STRAIN hatch has both media in play** (GAS pressure strain and a HEAT cold face): two descriptors, two frame sprites in ascending order, bowed rim for GAS and rim frost for HEAT (row 26); `dir` picks the side of each.
775	- **If a fuel puddle sits in a room below the freezing point** (`LSG:838`): nothing changes in the MVP; the `25 PUDDLE` descriptor stays and the puddle draws unfrozen, with no frozen hint (the Graph reserves that for VS-A). Coolant's frost fan is never drawn on a fuel stain (FT-30's routed `medium` question for a frozen non-coolant tank).
776	- **If a `1 LEAK/GAS` descriptor's `intensity_pm` is 0** (an isolated duct): zero pixels draw, by design (FT-18); the descriptor and its acoustic class still exist, and no cyan glow is requested while `intensity_pm` is 0 (row 1). The absence is the verdict: "O2 failure leaves no trail" (`ART:697`).
777	- **If an exposed DUCT leaks to EXTERIOR**: the stream draws out through the hull-run anchor as `1 LEAK/GAS` (FT-3, row 1); the compartment's own `AIRFLOW` and `ATMO_*` descriptors carry the draught and the thinning, each by its own row.
778	- **If a SEVERED fluid open end remains after salvage**: it draws its medium's leak row at the open end until `cap_port` ends the descriptor; an ELECTRIC cable end draws nothing unless a `2 SHORT` is live there (the `8 SEVERED` row of the table of record).
779	- **If a BREACH pre-stage descriptor were WORN rather than the mode-5 STRUCT the Graph now states** (`LSG:170`; a later Graph version regressing it): the hull hairline would not be drawn (FT-32) and the hull case would lose its consequence-channel Pillar 2 tell; the TICK acoustic class would be absent too. This cannot happen under the present Graph and is kept as the regression the build-time lint "every id has a row" and AC-71 guard. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
780	- **If a descriptor's `sev` rises on an aged subject** (a hull plate at sev 3 with `mode_steps` 300 rises to sev 4): the Graph resets the mode onset, so on the `N/` frame `grow_steps` is 0, the l head draws at `MIN_EXTENT_PX` and the extent regrows at 15 px per step (48, 48, 48, 48, 60, 75, ...); the previous, shorter-lived mark of the smaller size is replaced by the new head, never inflated (FT-8, T6). If `sev` falls, the same reset applies at the lower rate. This is the resolution adopted for the "a sev rise redraws hundreds of pixels of history in one frame" finding; it is a default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (Open Questions 6c), and neither the one-frame jump to the old age bound nor an `EXTENT_JUMP_MAX` cap is adopted. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
781	- **If a subject carries two live RUN descriptors** (a seam weep and a BREACH pre-stage; a FREEZE and a LEAK) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the Graph keeps one onset pair, for the dominant one (highest `sev`, ties to the lowest `mode`), and hands the other the legacy `since_steps`. The resolver draws the non-dominant NODE or EDGE descriptor as its head stamp only (`MIN_EXTENT_PX`, `dull_step` 0) and the non-dominant seam weep at its true `built_step` age, so no frame inflates (FT-8, AC-181). It is never undrawn.
782	- **If a leak appears or clears in a room that already shows `20 ATMO_COLD` frost at a constant `T`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: no patch moves, appears or disappears, because the room-frost anchor tile is fixed by Layout geometry alone (FT-11, D.2b, AC-182).
783	- **If a derelict dead fault is back-dated** (Derelict Authoring DA-17, which must seed all three GA-T fields, Open Questions 25): the section is instantiated with `mode_since_step` (and `fail_since_step`) in the past, `mode_key` set to the fault's key and `isolated_at_step` 0, so `grow_steps` and `mode_steps` are large, the extent is the whole edge and `dull_step` is the dried stop once `mode_steps` >= `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`; a `mode_since_step` seeded without its `mode_key` is overwritten by the Graph's phase 9 on the first run and the fault is born fresh (FT-8); a back-date that sets only `fail_since_step` leaves `mode_steps` at 0, so every dead fault would be born `dull_step` 0 with extent 48 (the authoring lint `DEAD_FAULT_NOT_DRIED` must read `mode_steps`; cross-GDD note). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
784	- **If a tank of fuel freezes** (`4 FREEZE`, `medium` FUEL, `LSG:170`): the frost sheath draws on the tank's lagging in Coolant Ice with no fan and no drip; no coolant fan is drawn on it (row 4, FT-12). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
785	- **If a trail's source is off-screen but its body crosses the view** (an anchor behind the camera edge, a 600 px run entering the field): the trail is drawn that frame, because the test is the polyline bounding box padded by one head cell, not the anchor (FT-19, AC-154). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
786	- **If the room warms or cools across the FROST edge at 8 mC per step** (room frost, row 20): the patch count rises by at most one patch per Graph step (D.2b pop bound, AC-148); at the first FROST step exactly one patch (the anchor tile's) appears, so a sev-2 descriptor is never undrawn (FT-19) and never pops across the room. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
787	- **If a coolant leak sits in a COMFORT room** (the home-ship default, frost reach 0): the chain is the head fan stamp followed by the wet run to the age-bound extent (D.2d); `frost_px` is 0, the drip runs, and the width steps 8 / 6 / 4 / 2 px with distance from the source, so the wound is followable at every temperature; a sev 3 six-tile run is complete at `grow_steps` 48 (4.8 s), and a valve closing freezes it with the extent (FT-8). Nothing changes with temperature except which pieces are frost. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
788	- **If a derelict dead coolant fault sits in a COMFORT room**: it draws the head fan stamp and the whole run greyed, with no drip (STILL, back-dated, dulled by `mode_steps`, D.5, D.2d); the coolant verdict reads at any temperature, not only in a cold room. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
789	- **If a LIVE descriptor's `mode_steps` is at or above `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`** (a leak isolated early and reopened; default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), Open Questions 6d): it is shown at stop `DULL_STEPS` - 2 and `fuel_dried` stays false; when the valve next closes the descriptor is STILL, the cap releases and the stop steps to the dried stop in one frame (one palette step, intended: the pipe is old and the step follows the player's own valve; AC-177). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
790	- **If a closed door lets an unheated room cool** (Graph ruling D12, default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20)): rooms behind closed doors cool to COOL and FROST in 20-30 minutes; the Graph rules this the intended consequence and not a warning, so this system adds nothing for it: the `20 ATMO_COLD` crust draws from the room's true `T` by D.2b exactly as for any other cold room. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
791	
792	### Degenerate strategies
793	
794	- **If the player zooms out to hide nothing, or in to hide something**: neither works. A trail is drawn whenever its padded polyline bounding box meets the field at the current ladder step k (FT-19; the anchor point is not the test) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; off-field trails are re-evaluated at every k, so a zoom-out reveals every one and a zoom-in leaves no stale state (there is none to go stale).
795	- **If the player opens and closes a valve every Graph step**: the `F/` key fires each step, the descriptor toggles DRAWN_LIVE and DRAWN_STILL, and only the moving media (drip, mist) start and stop; the stamps never blink and no cost accumulates (T3, T4; one re-select per key per step, D.7). The physical effect (the leak runs on alternate steps) is the Graph's.
796	- **If the player cuts and re-welds a section to "reset" a mature fan**: the Graph discards and rebuilds the nodes (`T`, `SEC/` keys), the descriptor's mode onset restarts (`grow_steps` and `mode_steps` 0; the legacy `since_steps` also restarts), and the trail regrows from 48 px at the sev's rate. This is honest: a re-welded joint is a new joint. No trail is hidden, because the Graph, not this system, ended the old one. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
797	- **If the player stands a carried or placed object, a body or a crewmate on a floor trail**: the mark is drawn beneath actors by the band rule (FT-25) and is occluded by the object's sprite; the descriptor, its hiss and its draught still exist. Occlusion by world geometry is physical and is not suppression; this system never moves, hides or fades a stamp for readability.
798	- **If the room is dark** (no lamp, no fixture, no glow reaches the trail): no *non-emissive* trail pixel is brighter than the hull-floor tint (FT-26); the acoustic class, the band cues and the draught still tell; a live emissive element (scorch rim, ember edge) may be visible and is the subject of FT-27, not a leak. Darkness is honest; light is a decision.
799	- **If the player tries to read all trails from a glance at a gauge, map or schematic**: none exists. The only way to see a trail is to spend light and walk to where the lamp reaches (Player Fantasy, "cost of checking"; FT-4).
800	
801	### Save, restore, dormancy and co-op
802	
803	- **If a restore happens mid-cascade**: the Graph emits one `ALL` after `post_restore`; this system performs one full re-read reconciled against its pool within the same render frame (FT-16, T10). Extents are already grown (a pure function of `grow_steps`), dullness is already final, and moving media take their phase from `present_time`, so a mist does not "start" on load. Nothing was saved by this system (`SL:853`, `SL:1027`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
804	- **If a derelict section is instantiated** (`ALL`): its authored dead faults draw STILL, dulled to their back-dated `mode_steps` (T2); no live moving media appear unless the authored descriptor has `intensity_pm` > 0 (a wet derelict fault is allowed and must be authored as such). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
805	- **If a section is dormant**: it emits no descriptors (`LSG:822`), so no trail draws; on wake the Graph's M19 has advanced every subject's `mode_since_step` and non-zero `isolated_at_step` by the dormant interval (LS-17), so the trails reappear at the `grow_steps` and `mode_steps` the section ran, with no catch-up animation. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
806	- **If the kernel is PAUSED**: `present_time`, `tick_alpha` and the committed tick freeze together; extents and animation stop; nothing advances or fades (FT-1).
807	- **If the player dies and the game restarts from the last autosave** (the MVP death handling, owned by Save/Load): the load is a restore; the trail set rebuilds from one `ALL` and carries no memory of what was on screen at death. Anything that depended on that memory (a "seen" flag, a first-sight flourish) does not exist here.
808	- **If a MIRROR client receives descriptors** (VS-B): the co-op summary carries the intensity bucket, `since_steps`, `mode_steps` and `grow_steps` per active descriptor (`LSG:210`, LS-21), so the client draws the same extent and dullness as the HOST by the same resolver; there is no legacy branch (FT-33). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review.)*
809	- **If two co-op clients are on different ladder steps k or different displays**: each draws the same descriptors at the same base-px positions and extents (layout is in base px, FT-34); only the field and the on-screen pixel size differ. A trail never depends on any one client's camera except for which anchors are inside its field.
810	- **If a client reconnects or a late joiner arrives (VS-B)**: it receives the Graph's state as a restore and therefore a single `ALL`; no trail history is transmitted or needed.
811	
812	### Hallucination and the truth channel
813	
814	- **If the Perception Filter runs at its maximum stage** (violet bleed on pipe silhouettes, a distorted cone): every trail pixel is bit-identical with the Filter on or off (FT-2, `PIPE:989`); a violet pipe beside an unviolet frost fan is itself a tell (Player Fantasy, drift stage 3).
815	- **If the Filter's mask route is unavailable**: the Filter disables its own pass (`PIPE:735`) and this system does nothing different; it never branches on the Filter's state.
816	- **If a class (b) hallucination shows a machine whole and green while its outlet fitting leaks**: the body sprite and gauge are the module-body channel and may lie; the mist, fan or scorch at the fitting is anchored to the fitting, not the body, and is unchanged (FT-24, ET-5). The floor outranks the machine.
817	- **If a class (a) phantom entity appears to tear a duct**: it leaves no descriptor, so no mark; a **real** hidden entity that ruptures a hull plate leaves an ordinary BREACH or LEAK descriptor, drawn along the rib or seam like any breach with no variant by `cause` (FT-31). "Did it leave a mark?" costs a walk and light.
818	- **If a hidden entity's GOUGE lands on a duct or cable** (not a hull segment): the Graph surfaces it only as the WORN descriptor (module-body, corruptible) or as a LEAK; this system draws the LEAK if there is one and nothing for WORN. This is the routed truth-channel hole (FT-31); until the Graph owner closes it, MVP Horror restricts GOUGE to hull segments (binding on the Horror Entities GDD, FT-31). Pillar 4(a) is a joint guarantee of this GDD (Graph descriptors) and Horror Entities (web-grammar footprints); neither may assume the other covers every footprint kind.
819	- **If more than `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` 16 footprint writes arrive in a step** (global, across all callers; registry `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`): the Graph drops the excess, so this system only ever sees accepted effects; a trail never shows a footprint the Graph did not accept (FT-31).
820	
821	### Display, accessibility and the alarm
822	
823	- **If reduced motion is on**: every moving medium holds frame 0, its authored hold frame; direction, density, size, extent and dullness continue; `present_time` still advances; no trail, hairline or audio is suppressed (FT-28, `PIPE:847`). A mist that does not drift is still a mist because its form rule carries it.
824	- **If reduce flashing is on** (the first-launch default): arc pops are replaced by the held glow at `ARC_HELD_GLOW_PM` (600 permille of peak) with the four static spark-tip pixels lit (D.8b, FT-29); the SHORT scorch still draws; no trail disappears (FT-29). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
825	- **If both reduced motion and reduce flashing are on**: the arc is a steady glow on its hold frame; the scorch, its extent and its dullness are unchanged; the only difference from a live arc is the absence of pops.
826	- **If k = 1 at 2160p** (the field is 36 times the area of the default): every on-screen stamp is still drawn; pressure degrades moving media first (frame count, then density, then `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS` halving, then far-from-beam frame hold), never stamps (FT-19, D.9). A sev 1-2 hairline (a 2 px composite) may not resolve at k = 1; that is accepted and logged and is not a licence to cull or to add a marker (FT-34). The hull-fatigue tell is then carried by the TICK acoustic class of the flow-zero row 5 pre-stage at the descriptor's anchor (consequence channel, Adaptive Audio, FT-34); no marker or layer is added.
827	- **If the Alarm Red sweep passes a lit trail**: the sweep tints lit albedo toward red, so loop hue may lose fidelity under it; the trail still identifies by form and polarity (the five behaviours differ in greyscale: FT-12), and the trail is never itself drawn in the alarm colour (FT-4). Hue fidelity under the sweep is a Lighting spike item.
828	- **If the window is resized or the display scale changes at run time**: `k_auto` and the field change; the next frame re-evaluates which anchors are in the field from the poll cache. No key is needed and no state is migrated.
829	
830	### Layout, budget and engine
831	
832	- **If a wall fitting has no floor-run geometry from Layout**: the wall part draws alone and the missing run is a lint error (Layout owes the start and direction of the floor run: FT-13), not a silent fallback; the trail is never hidden for lacking a run.
833	- **If `anchor_geometry` returns nothing for a descriptor's anchor** (a Layout read fails after a weld): the source stamp draws at the descriptor's own `anchor` with extent `MIN_EXTENT_PX`, never hidden (FT-19), and one diagnostic line is written.
834	- **If a subject is DESTROYED (`hp` 0)** (Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-11): this system draws whatever descriptor the Graph emits for it and decides nothing about emission (FT-3). The Graph's transition row gives a DESTROYED subject sev 4 and, for a hull segment, BREACH at `A_HOLE_MAX` (`LSG:242`), so `seg_b_breach` at `hp` 0 draws at size l (bent rib or hole) by row 5, and in its dried form once `intensity_pm` is 0 and `mode_steps` >= `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS`. If the Graph emits no descriptor for a DESTROYED subject, nothing is drawn (no decal, FT-3) and Derelict Authoring's fallback applies. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
835	- **If a floor run reaches a doorway or a room boundary**: the run stops at the sill; no opaque pixel is drawn in the neighbouring compartment (FT-37). This is Layout's rule (LY-8 e): a run that would cross is the Layout lint `FLOOR_RUN_CROSSES_BOUNDARY`, never a runtime clip.
836	- **If a wall fitting sits within 72 px of a door or cap seam**: the wall part is cropped to its host face and never drawn into the cap band (FT-13, `ART:1033`).
837	- **If `stamps_world` exceeds `TRAIL_MAX_STAMPS` 704, or the wall rows exceed `WALL_ROWS_MAX` 16, or an in-play `ALL` exceeds `TRAIL_RECONCILE_BUDGET_MS` 4 (a restore `ALL` exceeds `TRAIL_RESTORE_BUDGET_MS` 8)**: one diagnostic line is logged on the rising edge (FT-41 rule 5); every trail keeps drawing (a logging threshold, never a cut-off: FT-16, FT-19); the Pipeline's per-row z-band remedy applies to the Y-sorted layer, never fewer trails. The pool, pre-sized to `TRAIL_MAX_STAMPS`, grows past it and logs. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*
838	- **If `ALL` follows a 300-node breach**: one full re-read in the same frame (FT-16); the cost is D.7's `cost_all_us`; if it exceeds the threshold it is logged and the frame is not skipped.
839	- **If a particle path is used for venting and the spike has not passed**: it is not used; venting is stepped frames (FT-21). If the spike later passes, the 12-particle-emitter cap applies and exceeding it degrades moving media by the FT-19 order.

Result: no invariant breaks; GA-T is adopted"), so the contingency of the earlier text has lapsed and the legacy fallback is deleted. The Graph persists **three** onset fields per node, edge and seam, `mode_since_step`, `mode_key` and `isolated_at_step` (LS-21), and derives the two descriptor fields from them: `mode_steps = step_no - mode_since_step` (the age of the dominant descriptor's current mode and severity, restamped whenever `mode_key` = `(mode << 3) | sev` changes) and `grow_steps = max(0, (isolated_at_step if isolated_at_step > 0 else step_no) - mode_since_step)` (`mode_steps` frozen at the isolation step); COMPARTMENT and OPENING descriptors read 0 for both. The rule is **dominant-on

The vacuum-breach issue still isn't fixed or documented in this GDD — there's no mention of vacuum or the OQ. At severity-4, a breach with an open hole stays permanently live, and debris/wind streaks animate based on hole-area fraction alone, with no check for whether there's actually air to flow. That means on a ship that's already vacuum, the hull would still animate debris as if air were escaping.

I'll keep this as recommended but note CD wants it prerequisite for the Derelict B content story, and the G6 pass never addressed it. My fix proposal: either have Graph publish flow-based intensity when gas is present, or have F&T gate the moving media on compartment pressure being above zero, since it can read compartment() directly — this keeps it reader-compatible with a clear live predicate based on actual pressure differential.

This doesn't affect the AC-186 mapping. Now I need to move on to the Tuning Knobs section, then skim V/A, Game feel, Cross-References, ACs C-L, and the OQ — starting with tuning knobs.

### D.1b bead_segments *(added 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D39, default applied confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20))*

The bead_segments formula is defined as:

`bead_segments(h) = clamp(1 + floor(2 * (h - LEAK_HP) / (PATCH_CAP_BP - LEAK_HP)), 1, 3)`, where `h` is the patched subject's true `hp`, read live by the Module-Body Presenter (In-World Instruments IW-18) through the Graph's LS-19 `node_hp(id)` (the `hp` field of `edge(id)` for an edge). For the whole `PATCH_DECAY_S` 240 s hold `h` equals the banked hp at the end of the patch, completed or cancelled; after the hold it falls with the Graph's wear (100 bp per 10 s) and the bead shortens. Interaction never reads it, never in `validate` (IA-11a), and calls no mutator. The bead is drawn on the patch plate (module-body, IW-18), not by Failure & Trail: FT-32's `27 PATCH_WEEP` is one static POINT_FIXED mark per medium with no length axis and is identical for all three bead lengths. Checks at registry defaults (`LEAK_HP` 4000, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000, span 2000): `h` 4000 → 1 + floor(0) = 1; 4999 �

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `h` | int bp | 4000..6000 for a patched subject (a cancel before the first block leaves `h` unchanged) | the Graph's true `hp` | banked hp when the patch ended |
| `LEAK_HP` | int bp | 4000 | registry (cited) | hp at which the LEAK clears |
| `PATCH_CAP_BP` | int bp | 6000 | registry (cited) | the PATCH ceiling |
